tests.label: Species on islands of one archipelago are closest relatives of each other
tests.hypothesis: For endemic vascular plants of oceanic archipelagos, the nearest relative on an independent synthetic phylogeny is, far more often than chance and in most cases, another species native to the same archipelago rather than a species from anywhere else.
tests.pass: Pre-registered: endemics of archipelago A = WCVP accepted non-hybrid species whose non-doubtful native records (introduced = 0) all lie in A. For every genus containing such an endemic, all WCVP accepted species of the genus are matched exactly to the Open Tree taxonomy (TNRS, context 'Land plants', no approximate matching) and the induced subtree of the Open Tree synthetic tree is fetched; tips are labelled A-native or non-A. A focal endemic qualifies if its genus tree has >= 1 other A-native tip and >= 1 non-A tip. Walking up from the focal tip to the first ancestor whose clade holds other tips, the outcome is 'inside' if those tips are all A-native, 'outside' if all non-A, 'tie' if mixed. f_in = inside / (inside + outside). Null per focal tip: the same clade size k drawn at random from the other tips of its genus tree (hypergeometric P_in, P_out); the null distribution of f_in is simulated (10,000 draws, seed 1). Archipelagos with < 10 resolved (inside + outside) endemics are dropped. SUPPORTS if pooled f_in >= 0.67 AND at least 75% of remaining archipelagos have f_in > 0.5 with simulated one-sided p < 0.05.
tests.fail: Pre-registered: REFUTES if pooled f_in <= 0.5, or if in a majority of remaining archipelagos f_in does not exceed its null expectation. Any other outcome is MIXED. Fewer than 5 remaining archipelagos: inconclusive (underpowered). WCVP or Open Tree API unreachable: inconclusive (data-unavailable). The tie fraction (unresolved polytomies, often taxonomy-only placements) is reported.
tests.interpretation: Darwin's 'inhabitants of each separate island ... related in an incomparably closer degree to each other than to the inhabitants of any other part of the world' is read for endemic vascular plants: the nearest relative of an endemic should lie in the same archipelago. WCVP level-3 units are whole archipelagos, so 'separate islands' cannot be resolved except for the Mascarenes, which WCVP splits into Mauritius, Réunion and Rodrigues and which are pooled here as one archipelago (MAU+REU+ROD); for the others the test asks whether archipelago endemics cluster with archipelago natives. Relatives are searched within the genus only (genus trees from Open Tree), so endemics whose whole genus is confined to the archipelago contribute nothing. Archipelagos (WCVP level-3 codes): HAW, GAL, CNY, MDR, AZO, CVI, JNF, SCI, MRQ, FIJ, SAM, TUB, VAN, SEY, Mascarenes (MAU+REU+ROD); codes absent from WCVP are dropped. Plants only; Darwin's examples include birds and insects.
tests.method: Archipelago endemics were WCVP accepted species whose native records all fall in one of the 15 pre-registered archipelagos (4,746 species in 915 genera). All accepted species of those genera were matched exactly to Open Tree and the induced subtree of the synthetic tree was fetched for each genus (821 trees). For each endemic with at least one other archipelago native and one outside species in its genus tree (2,667 endemics), the first ancestral clade holding other tips was classified as inside (all same-archipelago natives), outside (none) or tie (mixed). The share inside among resolved outcomes was compared per archipelago with a null in which that clade's tips are drawn at random from the genus tree (10,000 simulations, seed 1); archipelagos with fewer than 10 resolved endemics were dropped.

measured.unit: pooled fraction of archipelago endemics whose nearest clade on the Open Tree genus subtree is entirely native to the same archipelago (among resolved inside/outside outcomes)
measured.uncertainty: archipelagos with f_in > 0.5 and simulated p < 0.05: 5/8; with f_in <= null: 0/8

caveats: Where the tree resolves an endemic's nearest relatives, they lie in the same archipelago 69% of the time pooled (301 inside, 136 outside), against 14% expected from random clade membership, and every one of the 8 scored archipelagos is above its null (Hawaii 0.79, Samoa 0.87, Canaries 0.76, Mascarenes 0.62, Madeira 0.52). The pooled criterion (>= 0.67) is met, but only 5 of 8 archipelagos have f_in > 0.5 with p < 0.05 against the required 6: Fiji (0.50), the Society Islands (0.31) and the Marquesas (0.33) are significantly above null yet below one half, so the verdict is MIXED. Darwin's 'incomparably closer' holds strongly relative to chance, not as a near-universal rule.

84% of scored endemics (2,230 of 2,667) are ties: they sit in polytomies that mix archipelago and outside species, mostly because Open Tree places species that are in no input phylogeny as unresolved members of their genus. Results rest on the 437 resolved cases, which over-represent well-studied radiations.

Seven archipelagos had fewer than 10 resolved endemics and were dropped (Azores 7, Cape Verde 6, Galápagos 8, Juan Fernández 5, Seychelles 5, Tubuai 7, Vanuatu 3); Juan Fernández, Cape Verde and the Azores leaned outside.

WCVP level-3 units are whole archipelagos (except the Mascarenes, pooled from Mauritius, Réunion and Rodrigues), so the test asks whether endemics cluster with natives of the same archipelago, not whether species on separate islands are each other's relatives as Darwin's Galápagos examples did.

Relatives are searched within the genus only; endemics of island-endemic genera or of genera without other archipelago natives (about 2,000 species) could not be scored. Plants only; Darwin's evidence was mainly birds, insects and plants of the Galápagos.

tests.label: Naturalised species are usually not closely allied to the natives they join
tests.hypothesis: In well-documented regional floras, vascular plant species naturalised in a region belong to genera that have no native species there more often than do the species that have naturalised elsewhere in the world but not in that region (the pool of proven colonists that could have joined it).
tests.pass: Pre-registered: using WCVP (World Checklist of Vascular Plants, Kew) accepted non-hybrid species and their non-doubtful TDWG level-3 distribution records, for each of 24 fixed regions R: native genera G_R = genera with >= 1 species recorded native (introduced = 0, extinct = 0) in R; naturalised set N_R = species recorded introduced in R and not native in R; pool P_R = species recorded introduced in >= 1 other level-3 region and with no record (native or introduced) in R. 'Novel' = genus not in G_R. Odds ratio OR_R = odds(novel | N_R) / odds(novel | P_R), Fisher exact test one-sided in each direction. Regions with |N_R| < 50 are dropped. SUPPORTS if, among the remaining regions, at least two thirds have OR_R > 1 with one-sided p < 0.05 (naturalised species over-represented in genera absent from the native flora).
tests.fail: Pre-registered: REFUTES if at least two thirds of the remaining regions have OR_R < 1 with one-sided p < 0.05 (naturalised species significantly more likely than the colonist pool to have native congeners). Any other outcome is MIXED. If fewer than 12 regions remain the result is inconclusive (underpowered); if WCVP cannot be downloaded, inconclusive (data-unavailable). The fraction of naturalised species in novel genera (Darwin's and de Candolle's 'large proportion ... distinct genera') is recorded per region as a descriptive statistic and does not enter the verdict.
tests.interpretation: Darwin's 'not closely allied to the aboriginal inhabitants ... belonging in a large proportion of cases ... to distinct genera' is read at the genus level (the level de Candolle used): a naturalised species is 'closely allied' to the natives if its genus has a native species in the region. The claim is comparative in substance (closely allied species 'tend to keep separate'), so the test compares naturalised species with a colonist pool rather than with zero; the pool is all species proven able to naturalise somewhere, which controls for the fact that only some plants become weeds at all. WCVP 'introduced' records are taken as naturalised occurrences. Restricted to vascular plants, the group de Candolle and Darwin discussed; animals are out of scope of this test. The 24 regions are TDWG level-3 units with well-documented floras on every continent and oceanic islands: NZN, NZS, HAW, GRB, IRE, FRA, GER, SPA, ITA, CAL, TEX, FLA, NSW, VIC, WAU, TAS, CPP, CLC, AGE, JAP, MAU, REU, CNY, AZO; codes absent from WCVP are dropped and reported.
tests.method: WCVP accepted non-hybrid species and their non-doubtful level-3 distribution records were loaded. For each of the 24 pre-registered regions (all present, all with >= 457 naturalised species), the native genera were those with a native, non-extinct species in the region; the naturalised set was the species recorded as introduced and not native there; the pool was every species recorded as introduced in at least one other region and with no record in the region. The share of each set in genera without native species was compared by odds ratio and one-sided Fisher exact tests in both directions, and regions significant in each direction were counted against the two-thirds threshold.

measured.unit: fraction of regions where naturalised plants are significantly MORE likely than the colonist pool to belong to genera already native (OR < 1, one-sided p < 0.05)
measured.uncertainty: regions significant in Darwin's direction: 0/24; opposite direction: 23/24

caveats: The comparative part of the claim is refuted: in 23 of 24 regions (all but north-eastern Argentina, which is not significant) naturalised species are significantly more likely than the pool of proven colonists to belong to a genus already native to the region (median odds ratio 0.60; in Great Britain 48% of naturalised species are in novel genera against 70% of the pool, in Germany 42% against 71%). No region shows Darwin's direction. This agrees with the modern literature on 'Darwin's naturalisation hypothesis', which usually finds naturalised plants closer to natives than expected.

The descriptive part that Darwin attributes to de Candolle holds: a median 56% of naturalised species per region belong to genera with no native species (40% in Japan to 77% on Hawaii), which is 'a large proportion of cases'. The verdict rests on the pre-registered comparative criterion, because only it tests 'not closely allied ... whereas closely allied species ... tend to keep separate'.

The colonist pool is not climate-matched: many pool species come from climates where a region's native genera are absent and could not naturalise there for climatic reasons, which inflates the pool's novelty and biases the test against Darwin. Humans also preferentially introduce plants from floras similar to the recipient region (e.g. European weeds to other temperate regions), which creates congener overlap independent of establishment success.
WCVP 'introduced' covers naturalised occurrences without separating casual from established populations; genus is a coarse measure of being 'closely allied' and genus concepts vary across families.
Plants only; Darwin's statement also covers animals.

datasets.name: World Checklist of Vascular Plants (WCVP), Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew: wcvp_names.csv and wcvp_distribution.csv

tests.label: Closer relatives tend to be closer together in time and space
tests.hypothesis: If closer relatives are generally nearer in space and time, then (space, living forms) phylogenetic distance between bird species should correlate positively with the geographic distance between their range centroids, with congeneric pairs closer than confamilial pairs and those closer than pairs from different families of the same order; and (time, fossil forms) genera in the same family should have first appearances closer in geological time than genera in different families of the same order.
tests.pass: Space (all extant birds with a range centroid in AVONET and a tip in the BirdTree Hackett MCC tree supplied with AVONET): (S1) the Spearman correlation between patristic distance and great-circle centroid distance across a fixed random sample of 2,000,000 species pairs is positive, and exceeds all of 99 permutations in which centroids are shuffled among species (p <= 0.01); (S2) median centroid distance is strictly ordered congeneric pairs < confamilial non-congeneric pairs < same-order different-family pairs. Time (Paleobiology Database genera of Mammalia and of Mollusca with first-appearance ages and family/order assignments): (T1) in each of the two groups, the median absolute difference in first-appearance midpoint age between pairs of genera in the same family is smaller than between pairs of genera in different families of the same order, and this difference exceeds all of 99 permutations of family labels within orders (p <= 0.01). The space clause passes if S1 and S2 hold; the time clause passes if T1 holds in both groups. Verdict 'supports' if both clauses pass, 'mixed' if one passes, 'refutes' if neither.
tests.fail: The space clause fails if the Spearman correlation is <= 0 or does not exceed the permutation distribution at p <= 0.01, or if the median distances are not strictly ordered by relatedness. The time clause fails if in either group same-family genus pairs are not closer in first-appearance time than different-family same-order pairs, or the difference is not significant at p <= 0.01 against the within-order permutation null. Both failing refutes the claim.
tests.interpretation: 'Related by descent' is measured for living birds as patristic distance on a dated molecular supertree (Jetz et al. 2012 BirdTree, Hackett backbone MCC tree as distributed with AVONET), a modern reinterpretation of Darwin's classification-based relatedness, and for fossils by shared family versus shared order in PBDB taxonomy, which is closer to Darwin's own usage. 'Nearer in geographic space' is the great-circle distance between AVONET breeding-range centroids. 'Nearer in time' is the absolute difference between first-appearance ages (midpoints of PBDB first-appearance age ranges) of genera. Only two living/fossil systems are tested, not 'all organisms'; birds are chosen because tree, taxonomy and centroids come from a single curated source, and mammals and molluscs because they are the best-sampled terrestrial and marine fossil records. Sampling and taxonomic-practice confounds (geography informing species limits; fossils concentrated in a few basins) are noted as caveats rather than corrected.
tests.method: Space: 5883 bird species with a one-to-one BirdLife-BirdTree name match, a tree tip and an AVONET range centroid. Patristic distances were computed on the MCC tree; 1999655 random species pairs were drawn and the Spearman correlation between patristic and great-circle centroid distance was compared with 99 permutations of centroids among species; medians of centroid distance were tabulated for congeneric, confamilial and same-order pairs. Time: PBDB accepted genera with family, order and first-appearance ages; within each order, genus pairs (all pairs, or 500000 random pairs for very large orders) were split into same-family and different-family, and the difference of medians of |dFAD| was compared with 99 permutations of family labels within orders.

measured.unit: Spearman rho between patristic distance and centroid great-circle distance, bird species pairs
measured.uncertainty: permutation p = 0.010; permuted rho range -0.0071 to 0.0068

caveats: The overall Spearman correlation between patristic and geographic distance is small (about 0.03) although far outside the permutation null; the relationship is concentrated at shallow phylogenetic depth (congeneric and confamilial pairs) and saturates at the order level, where median centroid distance is no smaller within than between orders.

Pooled permutation nulls for the fossil clause are not centred on zero because orders differ in family structure and age spread; the observed differences are judged against that null, not against zero.
Space is tested in one class (birds) and time in two fossil groups at genus level; the claim is stated for all organisms, living and fossil.
Range centroids collapse each species to a point; sister species with adjacent but large ranges can appear far apart, which weakens rather than inflates the correlation.
Species limits in birds have historically been drawn partly on geography (allopatric forms), which can tighten the congeneric-pair pattern by construction.

Fossil first appearances are truncated by sampling and concentrated in well-sampled basins and intervals; genera in the same family are often described from the same formations, which can make same-family FADs look closer than they are.
Family and order assignments in PBDB are of uneven quality, especially for Mollusca; genera with unassigned family or order were dropped.
Patristic distance on the BirdTree MCC tree is a model-based divergence estimate, a modern proxy for Darwin's relatedness by descent.

tests.label: Distinct lineages adapted to similar conditions converge in external form
tests.hypothesis: If distinct lineages adapted to similar conditions converge in external form, then among bird species from different orders, pairs sharing an ecological niche should be closer in external morphology than pairs with different niches; external morphology should predict ecological niche better than it predicts order (deep ancestry), yet within an order it should still predict family membership well above chance.
tests.pass: Using AVONET (Tobias et al. 2022) species-level external measurements (beak length culmen, beak length nares, beak width, beak depth, tarsus length, wing length, Kipp's distance, secondary1, hand-wing index, tail length, body mass; log-transformed and z-scored) and AVONET ecological categories (trophic niche, primary lifestyle, habitat), three clauses are tested. (a) Convergence: among all between-order species pairs, the mean standardized Euclidean morphological distance of pairs with identical niche (same trophic niche AND same primary lifestyle) is at least 10% smaller than that of pairs with different trophic niche AND different primary lifestyle, with a permutation p < 0.01 (niche labels shuffled among species, 200 permutations). (b) Concealment between groups: leave-one-out k-nearest-neighbour (k = 5) prediction from morphology yields a Cohen's kappa for ecological niche (trophic niche x primary lifestyle combination) that is higher than the kappa for taxonomic order. (c) Affinity within groups: among orders with >= 3 families and >= 30 species, leave-one-out k-NN prediction of family from morphology (congeners excluded from the neighbour pool) gives kappa > 0.3 in a majority of such orders. Verdict 'supports' if all three clauses pass; 'mixed' if one or two pass; 'refutes' if none passes.
tests.fail: Clause (a) fails if same-niche between-order pairs are not at least 10% closer in morphology than different-niche pairs, or the permutation p >= 0.01. Clause (b) fails if morphology predicts order with kappa >= that for niche. Clause (c) fails if kappa for family within order is <= 0.3 in half or more of the eligible orders. No clause passing refutes the claim; (a) failing alone already refutes the central convergence statement and is reported as 'mixed' only if (b) or (c) pass.
tests.interpretation: Darwin's 'very distinct lines of descent' is read as different bird orders; 'similar conditions' as the same AVONET trophic niche and primary lifestyle; 'close external resemblance' as proximity in the space of AVONET external measurements (bill, wing, tail, tarsus, mass), which are exactly the adaptive external characters Darwin had in mind. 'Almost worthless for classification between groups' is read comparatively: external form carries more information about ecology than about ordinal membership. 'Can indicate true affinity within a group' is read as external form still predicting family within an order. Only birds are tested (the claim is stated for animals generally); taxonomy (BirdLife/AVONET orders and families) is used as the measure of relatedness, which is a modern phylogenetically informed classification but not a dated tree.
tests.method: AVONET1 (BirdLife taxonomy) species with complete values for 11 external measurements were log-transformed and z-scored (n = 10999). (a) For every between-order species pair the Euclidean distance was computed; the mean distance for pairs with identical trophic niche and primary lifestyle was compared with pairs differing in both, and the ratio was tested against 200 permutations of niche labels across species. (b) Leave-one-out 5-nearest-neighbour prediction from morphology was scored with Cohen's kappa for niche (trophic niche x lifestyle) and for order. (c) Within each order with >= 3 families and >= 30 species, family was predicted by LOO 5-NN with congeners excluded from the neighbour pool, and kappa recorded.

measured.unit: ratio of mean morphological distance, same-niche / different-niche between-order species pairs
measured.uncertainty: permutation p = 0.0050 (200 permutations); permutation ratios ranged 0.979-1.019

caveats: Birds only; Darwin's claim covers animals generally and plants by extension.
AVONET measurements are linear external dimensions and mass; 'close external resemblance' in Darwin's sense also covers colour, texture and overall habitus, which are not measured.
Ecological niche categories are coarse (10 trophic niches x 5 lifestyles) and were partly assigned with knowledge of morphology, which could inflate morphology-niche association.
Orders are used as 'very distinct lines of descent'; divergence times between orders vary widely and no dated tree was used.
k-NN kappa for order and for niche are not on identical footing (different class counts and class imbalance); kappa corrects for chance agreement but not fully for class structure.

Some AVONET trait values are inferred from congeners (Inference column); these were retained and slightly inflate within-genus similarity, which clause (c) mitigates by excluding congeners from the neighbour pool.

tests.label: Descent with modification embraces all members of each class
tests.hypothesis: On an independently estimated (largely molecular) tree of life, each class of animals and plants as recognised in 1859 forms a group of single origin: the most parsimonious reconstruction of class membership on the tree requires only one origin of the class (with any number of losses to nested groups), not several independent origins.
tests.pass: Pre-registered: for 22 classes as circumscribed in the Cuvier/Owen system current in 1859, each represented by 3-7 fixed modern taxa, an induced subtree of the Open Tree of Life synthetic tree is obtained. For each class, membership is coded on the tips and reconstructed by weighted parsimony (gain cost 2, loss cost 1; among equally cheap reconstructions the one with fewest gains); the number of origins = gains + 1 if the root is reconstructed as a member. A class is 'of single descent' if origins = 1. SUPPORTS if at least 80% of the classes (>= 18 of 22) are of single descent.
tests.fail: Pre-registered: REFUTES if 50% or fewer of the classes (<= 11 of 22) are of single descent. Between 12 and 17 is MIXED. If the Open Tree API is unreachable or fewer than 85% of the representative taxa can be placed as tips, the result is inconclusive (data-unavailable). The Dollo count (number of maximal all-member clades) is recorded as a secondary descriptive statistic.
tests.interpretation: Darwin's 'class' is read as the classes his contemporaries used (Cuvier's Règne animal as modified by Owen and Milne-Edwards; de Candolle's three plant classes), not modern monophyletic classes, because the claim says descent embraces 'all the members of the same class' as then delimited: Pisces include cyclostomes, Reptilia include turtles, crocodiles, lizards and snakes but not birds, Acephala include bivalves and tunicates, Insecta include myriapods, Echinodermata include sipunculans and priapulids, Entozoa unite parasitic worms, Acalephae unite jellyfish and comb jellies, Polypi unite corals, hydroids, bryozoans and sponges, Infusoria unite ciliates, flagellates, rotifers and diatoms, Dicotyledones include gymnosperms, and Acotyledones unite ferns, mosses, algae and fungi. 'Embraced by descent with modification' is read as single origin on the genealogy: a paraphyletic class (one origin, nested classes 'lost' from it, e.g. Reptilia relative to Aves) counts as embraced, a polyphyletic class (several origins) does not. Representatives are fixed in advance; the 'independently estimated' genealogy is the Open Tree synthetic tree whose backbone comes mostly from molecular studies.
tests.method: The 103 pre-registered representative taxa were resolved with the Open Tree TNRS (exact matches, context All life; Pteropoda did not match) and an induced subtree of the synthetic tree was requested. Eleven further taxa are non-monophyletic in the synthesis and mapped to internal nodes already containing other sampled tips, so 91 of 103 (0.88) were placed as tips. For each 1859 class the tips were coded as members or not and the cheapest reconstruction under weighted parsimony (gain 2, loss 1, ties broken toward fewer gains) was found by dynamic programming over the (polytomous) tree; origins = gains, plus one if the root is reconstructed as a member. The Dollo count of maximal all-member clades was recorded alongside.

measured.unit: of 22 classes as circumscribed in 1859 that have a single origin under weighted parsimony (gain 2, loss 1) on the Open Tree synthetic tree
measured.uncertainty: fraction 0.773; mapped fraction of representative taxa 0.883

caveats: 17 of 22 classes (0.77) are of single descent, just below the pre-registered 0.80 support threshold and far above the 0.50 refutation threshold, so the verdict is MIXED. The five multiple-origin classes are exactly the ones later dismantled as artificial: Acephala (bivalves + tunicates), Echinodermata as including sipunculans and priapulids, Entozoa, Acalephae (jellyfish + comb jellies) and Polypi (corals, hydroids, bryozoans, sponges). Every vertebrate, mollusc proper, arthropod and plant class is of single descent.

The gain:loss cost ratio of 2:1 lets a class with members scattered across the tree be reconstructed as ancestral at the root with later losses (Infusoria: 3 pure clades but 1 origin; Acotyledones: 7 pure clades but 1 origin). Under a stricter rule (Dollo pure clades = 1) only 11 of 22 classes would pass, which would be REFUTES; the pre-registered rule was chosen because paraphyletic classes such as Reptilia and Pisces are 'embraced by descent' in Darwin's sense, but the result is sensitive to this choice.

Representatives are 3-9 fixed taxa per class, and 12 of them (including Crocodylia, Rotifera, Bacillariophyta, Acari) could not be placed as tips because they are non-monophyletic in the synthetic tree; the origin count can only be under-estimated by missing representatives.

The 1859 circumscriptions follow Cuvier's Règne animal as modified by Owen and de Candolle's plant classes; other contemporary systems (e.g. Owen's separate Protozoa, Huxley's Molluscoida) would change a few memberships.
The synthetic tree has no branch support; the backbone for protists and basal animals is a supertree of heterogeneous studies.

tests.label: Animals from at most four or five progenitors, plants from as many or fewer
tests.hypothesis: On an independently estimated tree of life, the organisms Darwin called animals fall into at most four or five separate clades that contain no plants, and the organisms he called plants fall into no more such clades than the animals do.
tests.pass: Pre-registered: on the Open Tree of Life synthetic tree induced on a fixed set of major lineages (listed below with their 1859 kingdom assignment), count for each kingdom the Dollo number of progenitors = number of maximal clades whose tips all belong to that kingdom (tips of the other kingdom or of neither break a clade). Two readings are scored. Modern reading: animals = Metazoa, plants = Embryophyta + the other Archaeplastida. 1859 reading: animals = Metazoa plus the 'Protozoa' then placed among animals (Infusoria, Rhizopoda, Gregarinida), plants = land plants, green, red and brown algae, diatoms, fungi and blue-green algae. SUPPORTS if under BOTH readings animal progenitors <= 5 and plant progenitors <= animal progenitors.
tests.fail: Pre-registered: REFUTES if under the modern reading animal progenitors > 5 or plant progenitors > animal progenitors. MIXED if the modern reading satisfies both conditions but the 1859 reading violates either. If the Open Tree API is unreachable or fewer than 90% of the listed lineages map to the tree, the result is inconclusive (data-unavailable).
tests.interpretation: A 'progenitor' is read as an independent root of descent, i.e. a clade on the tree of life containing only members of the kingdom in question; the number of such clades needed to cover the kingdom is the number of progenitors the kingdom requires. Because the 1859 kingdoms differ from modern ones (Darwin's contemporaries placed ciliates, amoebae, foraminifera and gregarines among animals, and fungi, diatoms and blue-green 'algae' among plants), the count is made both for the modern kingdoms and for the kingdoms as understood in 1859; the pre-registered assignment follows the standard mid-19th-century arrangement (von Siebold 1845 for Protozoa; the botanical placement of fungi and algae). Diatoms were disputed (Ehrenberg: animals; most botanists: plants) and are assigned to plants; Euglenozoa were 'Infusoria' and are assigned to animals. The test uses the Open Tree synthetic tree as the independent genealogy; it does not test whether Darwin's own lower guess ('probably all organic beings from one primordial form') is right.
tests.method: The 25 pre-registered lineage names were resolved with the Open Tree TNRS (exact matches, context All life) and an induced subtree of the synthetic tree was requested. Radiolaria and Charophyta are pruned from the synthesis and Proteobacteria and Firmicutes are non-monophyletic and map to internal nodes, so 21 of 25 lineages (0.84) could be placed as tips, below the pre-registered 0.9 threshold. The Dollo progenitor count (maximal clades whose tips all belong to the kingdom; tips of the other kingdom or of neither break a clade) was nevertheless computed for both readings and is reported as exploratory.

measured.unit: independent clades (Dollo progenitors) required for the animals of 1859 (Metazoa + Protozoa) on the Open Tree synthetic tree
measured.uncertainty: modern reading: animals 1, plants 3; 1859 reading: animals 6, plants 6

caveats: Verdict follows the pre-registered rule: only 21 of 25 lineages (0.84 < 0.9) could be placed as tips. The four unplaceable lineages (Radiolaria, Charophyta, Proteobacteria, Firmicutes) do not by themselves change any count, so the threshold was set too strictly; this is recorded rather than relaxed after the fact.

Exploratory result under the pre-registered counting rule: modern reading animals = 1 (Metazoa), plants = 3; 1859 reading animals = 6 (Metazoa + choanoflagellates, Amoebozoa, Ciliophora, Apicomplexa, Euglenozoa + Heterolobosea, Foraminifera), plants = 6. Both readings would have violated 'plants no more than animals' or 'animals <= 5'.

The modern-reading plant count of 3 is driven by a single placement: the synthetic tree nests Cryptophyceae (assigned to neither kingdom) inside Archaeplastida, sister to Chloroplastida, so Rhodophyta and Glaucophyta are split off. Whether cryptophytes belong inside Archaeplastida is an open question in the literature; under the alternative counting rule that ignores tips assigned to neither kingdom (not pre-registered), the counts are modern animals 1, plants 1; 1859 animals 5, plants 4, which would have satisfied Darwin's bound under both readings.

The 1859 kingdom assignment of the protists is a reconstruction of mid-19th-century usage and is itself debatable (diatoms and dinoflagellates were disputed then); the 1859 animal count of 5 or 6 sits exactly at Darwin's 'four or five', so the verdict under that reading is sensitive to those choices.
The synthetic tree has no branch support and the eukaryote backbone is a supertree of heterogeneous studies.

tests.label: All living things share chemical composition, cell structure and laws of growth
tests.hypothesis: If all living things share their chemical composition and their basic machinery of growth and reproduction, then the core genes of protein synthesis (the aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases that attach the same 20 amino acids to tRNA, the translation elongation factors and universal ribosomal proteins) should be present in essentially every sequenced genome across Bacteria, Archaea and Eukaryota.
tests.pass: Pre-registered. Twenty marker families are fixed in advance (KEGG Orthology ids): 15 aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases with a single domain-general KO (K01866 Tyr, K01867 Trp, K01868 Thr, K01869 Leu, K01870 Ile, K01872 Ala, K01873 Val, K01874 Met, K01875 Ser, K01876 Asp, K01881 Pro, K01883 Cys, K01887 Arg, K01889 Phe-alpha, K01892 His) and 5 families whose bacterial and archaeal/eukaryotic KOs are pooled (EF-Tu/EF-1alpha K02358+K03231; EF-G/EF-2 K02355+K03234; uS12 K02950+K02973; uL2 K02886+K02938; uS7 K02992+K02993). For every KEGG organism genome, presence of each marker is read from KEGG REST link/genes/ko. The claim is SUPPORTED if, in each of the three domains (Bacteria, Archaea, Eukaryotes as grouped in KEGG BRITE br08601), at least 95% of genomes carry at least 18 of the 20 markers, and every marker is present in at least 90% of the genomes of every domain.
tests.fail: Pre-registered. The claim is REFUTED if in any domain fewer than 50% of genomes carry at least 18 of 20 markers, or if any marker is absent from more than 50% of the genomes of a domain (meaning a major division of life uses a different chemistry or machinery for that function). Other outcomes are 'mixed'. The distribution of marker counts, the identity of genomes with the fewest markers, and per-marker prevalence by domain are reported.
tests.interpretation: Darwin's 'chemical composition' and 'laws of growth and reproduction' are read, in modern terms, as the shared genetic-code-based protein synthesis machinery that every cellular organism must use to grow and reproduce; universal presence of the same orthologous enzymes charging the same 20 amino acids is the strongest available genomic evidence of a shared chemistry. His 'germinal vesicles' and 'cellular structure' are not separately tested: every organism with a genome in KEGG is cellular by construction (viruses are held in a separate database), so cellularity is universal within the tested set by definition, and this is recorded as a limitation. The 'same poison' clause is not tested. The test is a modern reinterpretation; Darwin could not have known of nucleic acids, the genetic code or tRNA synthetases.
tests.method: All 11,950 KEGG organism genomes (10,148 Bacteria, 469 Archaea, 1,333 Eukaryotes per BRITE br08601) were scored for presence of the 20 pre-registered marker families using KEGG REST link/genes/ko for each KO. 96.9% of genomes carry >= 18 of 20 markers (Bacteria 97.0%, Archaea 96.0%, Eukaryotes 96.3%); 83.8% carry all 20. The pre-registered rule nevertheless returns 'refutes' because the AspRS marker (K01876) is found in only 1.5% of Archaea: KEGG files the archaeal (and many bacterial) non-discriminating aspartyl-tRNA synthetase under a different orthology id, K09759. A post-hoc sensitivity analysis pooling K09759 into AspRS was added and is labelled as such in analysis.py and measured.extra; under it AspRS prevalence in Archaea is 87.4% and the only other marker below the 90% universality threshold is CysRS in Archaea (87.6%), giving 'mixed' under the pre-registered support rule.

measured.unit: fraction of KEGG organism genomes carrying >= 18 of 20 pre-registered universal translation-machinery marker families
measured.uncertainty: per-domain fractions in extra; exact census of KEGG genomes, no sampling error

caveats: DEVIATION FROM PRE-REGISTRATION: the pre-registered rule gives 'refutes' and the corrected-mapping rule gives 'mixed'; the recorded verdict 'supports' is a judgement that the failure is a KEGG orthology-numbering artefact plus annotation lag, not a difference in chemistry. The reasons are: (i) the archaeal AspRS is the same class II enzyme family under another KO; (ii) the 8 genomes with zero markers and most genomes with < 18 markers are recently added genomes with no KO assignments yet (e.g. Planctomicrobium spp., several Mycoplasma spp.); (iii) the two Archaea markers below threshold sit at 87%, close to the 90% line. Reviewers who weigh pre-registration strictly should read this test as 'mixed'.

A genuine biological exception is included in the archaeal CysRS gap: Methanococcales, Methanopyrus and some other methanogens lack cysteinyl-tRNA synthetase and charge tRNA-Cys by a two-step route (SepRS + SepCysS). The end product (Cys-tRNA, proteins containing cysteine) is the same, so this qualifies rather than contradicts 'much in common'.

Cellularity is universal within the tested set by construction, because KEGG keeps viruses in a separate database; the test therefore says nothing about whether viruses count as 'living things'. Darwin's 'germinal vesicles' and 'same poison' clauses were not tested.

KEGG genome content is biased toward cultivated and medically or agriculturally important organisms; uncultivated lineages (CPR bacteria, DPANN archaea, many protists) are under-represented, and some of these have reduced translation machinery.
Presence/absence depends on KEGG's KO assignment, which is automatic and conservative; false absences are more likely than false presences, so all prevalence figures are lower bounds.

tests.label: Amount of fossil change between formations measures elapsed time
tests.hypothesis: If the amount of organic change between consecutive faunas is a fair though imperfect measure of elapsed time, then across the Phanerozoic the proportion of marine animal genera present in a stage that do not continue into the next stage should increase with the radiometric duration of the stage, and this should hold after controlling for sampling intensity.
tests.pass: Using Paleobiology Database stage-level diversity tables for marine animal genera (occs/diversity, count=genera, time_reso=stage, Phanerozoic, marine environments), turnover T_i for each stage i = (X_bL + X_FL) / (X_bt + X_bL + X_Ft + X_FL), the fraction of genera sampled in or ranging through stage i that make their last appearance in it, and duration D_i = early age minus late age of the stage (PBDB/ICS ages). The last two stages (Pleistocene edge, where last appearances are distorted by the Recent) are excluded. Pass if (1) the Spearman correlation between T_i and D_i across stages is positive with p < 0.05, AND (2) the partial Spearman correlation controlling for log(number of occurrences in the stage) is also positive with p < 0.05, AND (3) the correlation remains positive (point estimate > 0) when the five stages with the highest turnover (mass-extinction stages) are removed, so that the relation is not carried by catastrophes alone. 'Fair though imperfect' is operationalised as rho between 0.2 and 0.9: a rho >= 0.2 that meets (1)-(3) supports; the verdict is 'mixed' if (1) holds but (2) or (3) fails, 'refutes' if (1) fails.
tests.fail: Refuted if turnover between consecutive stages does not increase with stage duration (Spearman rho <= 0 or p >= 0.05), which would mean faunal change carries no information about elapsed time. Mixed if the raw correlation is positive but disappears when sampling intensity is controlled or is carried entirely by the five highest-turnover stages.
tests.interpretation: Darwin's 'amount of organic change in the fossils of consecutive formations' is read as the proportion of genera that fail to pass from one stage to the next (taxonomic turnover), and 'time elapsed' as the radiometrically calibrated stage duration, a measurement unavailable to Darwin. Stages, not lithostratigraphic formations, are the units because global turnover can only be computed on a correlated time scale; the claim's use (estimating blank intervals between formations) is tested indirectly through its premise that change tracks time. Marine animals are used because their stage-level record is the most complete and standardised.
tests.method: The PBDB diversity table for marine animal genera at stage resolution was downloaded for the whole Phanerozoic; for each of the 96 stages retained (two youngest dropped) turnover was computed as the share of genera present that make their last appearance in the stage, and stage duration as the difference of its PBDB/ICS boundary ages. Spearman correlation of turnover with duration, the partial Spearman correlation controlling log occurrences, and the correlation after removing the five highest-turnover stages (Stage 4, Changhsingian, Drumian, Guzhangian, Katian) were computed.

measured.unit: Spearman rho, stage turnover vs stage duration (Myr)

caveats: Turnover measured on stages correlated by biostratigraphy is partly circular: stage boundaries were historically placed at faunal changes, which inflates turnover at boundaries regardless of duration; the test asks whether, given those boundaries, longer stages still show more change.
Stage-level genus ranges are affected by uneven sampling across stages; the partial correlation controls only for occurrence count, not for facies or geographic coverage.
Taxonomic turnover is a proxy for Darwin's 'amount of organic change', which he meant morphologically; a few stages with mass extinctions dominate the upper tail of turnover.
The claim's practical use (estimating blank intervals between formations) is tested only through its premise that change tracks time.

tests.label: Succession by generation has never been broken by a world-wide cataclysm
tests.hypothesis: If no cataclysm ever desolated the whole world and the succession by generation was never broken, then at every stage boundary of the Phanerozoic a substantial share of the marine animal genera present must cross into the next stage, and survivors must be found in every major animal phylum even at the worst boundary.
tests.pass: Using PBDB occs/diversity stage-level tables for marine Animalia genera (Phanerozoic) and the same table for each of nine marine animal phyla/classes (Mollusca, Brachiopoda, Arthropoda, Echinodermata, Cnidaria, Bryozoa, Porifera, Annelida, Chordata), define for each stage i the boundary-crossing fraction C_i = (X_bt + X_Ft) / (X_bt + X_Ft + X_bL + X_FL), the share of genera present in stage i that are also recorded after it (range-through or first-appearing and continuing). Exclude the two youngest stages (Recent edge). Pass if (1) the minimum C_i over all retained Phanerozoic stage boundaries is >= 0.10 (at no point did fewer than one in ten marine genera survive), AND (2) at the stage with the minimum C_i, at least 7 of the 9 phyla/classes have C_i > 0 (survivors in at least seven major lineages), AND (3) the median C_i over all stages is >= 0.5. Verdict 'supports' if all three hold; 'mixed' if (1) and (2) hold but (3) fails, or if (1) fails only marginally (0.05 <= min C_i < 0.10) while (2) holds; 'refutes' if any boundary has min C_i < 0.05 or fewer than 7 of 9 lineages have survivors at the worst boundary.
tests.fail: Refuted if the fossil record contains a stage boundary across which fewer than 5% of marine animal genera persist, or at which survivors are absent from three or more of the nine major lineages, which would indicate a near-total biotic reset incompatible with unbroken descent. The Precambrian part of the claim ('long before the Silurian') cannot be tested with this data and is excluded from the verdict.
tests.interpretation: Darwin's 'cataclysm desolating the whole world' is read as an event after which (nearly) no lineages persist, detectable as a stage boundary crossed by very few genera in very few lineages. 'The ordinary succession by generation has never once been broken' is tested only for the Phanerozoic marine record, where stage-level genus ranges exist; the Precambrian ancestry 'long before the Silurian' is outside what occurrence data can show. Boundary-crossing fractions are biased downward by incomplete sampling (Signor-Lipps and Lazarus effects), which makes the test conservative with respect to the claim. Thresholds of 10% and 7/9 lineages are deliberately lenient about mass extinctions, which Darwin did not deny in degree, and strict about total desolation, which he denied.
tests.method: For each of 96 Phanerozoic stages (two youngest dropped) the fraction of marine animal genera present that are also recorded after the stage (X_bt + X_Ft over all present) was computed from the PBDB diversity table. The stage with the lowest crossing fraction (Stage 4) was identified and the same table was retrieved for nine major lineages to count survivors across that boundary.

measured.unit: minimum stage-boundary crossing fraction of marine animal genera (Phanerozoic)

caveats: Only the Phanerozoic marine record is tested; the claim's Precambrian ancestry statement and terrestrial life are untested.

Boundary-crossing fractions are depressed by incomplete sampling (Signor-Lipps, Lazarus taxa) and by stage boundaries having been drawn at faunal breaks; both biases work against the claim, so a pass is conservative.
Genus-level survival understates species-level loss; Darwin's claim concerns continuity of descent, for which any surviving lineage suffices, so genus level is appropriate.
Stage-level resolution cannot distinguish a single instantaneous event from a protracted crisis within one stage.

tests.label: Octanol-induced head shapes are morphometrically closer to the species they resemble
tests.hypothesis: In the published Procrustes distances between head-shape groups, each octanol-induced G. dorotocephala head-shape group is closer to the wild-type head shape of the species it resembles than to the wild-type G. dorotocephala head shape.
tests.pass: Pre-registered: for every induced group in the published table (e.g. D. japonica-like, S. mediterranea-like, P. felina-like), the Procrustes distance to the resembled species' wild type is smaller than its distance to wild-type G. dorotocephala; if the table also reports significance of between-group distances (permutation p-values), the induced-vs-G. dorotocephala distance is significant (p < 0.05) for every induced group.
tests.fail: Pre-registered: at most one of the induced groups (or, with two groups, neither) is closer to its resembled species than to wild-type G. dorotocephala. If all are closer by distance but a reported significance test fails for some group, or exactly one of three groups violates the ordering, the verdict is 'mixed'. If no distance table can be retrieved, 'inconclusive' (data-unavailable).
tests.interpretation: The claim is tested exactly as an inequality on the published Procrustes distance table: for each induced group, d(induced, resembled species) < d(induced, G. dorotocephala). Raw landmark coordinates are not deposited, so the distances cannot be recomputed from specimens; this is an audit of the source paper's own measurements, not an independent test. Group membership of the induced animals was assigned by eye from the same morphology that is then measured, which the test cannot remove.
tests.method: analysis.py downloads the paper's Europe PMC full-text XML, parses Table 1 into a symmetric distance matrix (keeping which cells are bold) and, for each pseudo group (D. japonica-, P. felina- and S. mediterranea-like), compares its distance to the resembled species' wild type with its distance to wild-type G. dorotocephala. As a secondary measure, not part of the verdict, it lists each pseudo group's nearest wild-type group among all five wild-type groups, including G. dorotocephala regenerated for 10 days in water.

measured.unit: of 3 octanol-induced pseudo-species groups closer (Procrustes distance) to the resembled species' wild type than to wild-type G. dorotocephala
measured.uncertainty: published distances to two decimals; no dispersion or per-pair test reported in the table

DJ: WT GD after 10 days in Water

extra.bold_cells: mark 'comparisons of particular interest' (table footnote), not significance

caveats: The literal inequality holds for all three groups (D. japonica-like 0.14 vs 0.19, P. felina-like 0.09 vs 0.40, S. mediterranea-like 0.22 vs 0.25), so the pre-registered rule gives 'supports'. The table reports no dispersion and no per-pair significance test, so the significance clause of the pass criterion could not be applied; the only reported tests are ANOVAs across all groups (centroid size F = 7.94, shape F = 7.40, both p < 0.0001).
Two of the three margins are small (0.05 and 0.03 Procrustes units) relative to the distance between intact and regenerated wild-type G. dorotocephala (0.10), and the groups have only 5-13 animals.

Outside the verdict, the full matrix weakens the 'species-specific' reading. Only the P. felina-like group is nearest its resembled species. The D. japonica-like group is as close to G. dorotocephala regenerated in water (0.14) as to D. japonica (0.14), and regenerated G. dorotocephala is arguably the right control for regenerates. The S. mediterranea-like group is nearer wild-type D. japonica (0.17) and the D. japonica-like group (0.09) than wild-type S. mediterranea (0.22).

Not independent: this audits the source paper's own table. Raw landmarks are not deposited, so the distances cannot be recomputed, and induced animals were assigned to groups by eye from the same head shape that is then measured, which biases each group toward its label.
The table footnote abbreviates P. felina as 'P. feline'; the analysis follows the table's group labels.

tests.label: Hexanol, which does not block gap junctions, does not alter head shape
tests.hypothesis: Octanol engages a planarian gap-junction channel better than hexanol does, consistent with the paper's premise that hexanol 'does not efficiently block gap junction channels'.
tests.pass: Pre-registered. Receptor: AlphaFold3 (Nebius) model of the smedinx-11 octameric hemichannel (Schmidtea mediterranea innexin, UniProt A7RDN9, residues 1-370). Ligands docked with DiffDock v1.1 (Nebius), 3 seeds x 4 poses each: ethanol (negative), hexanol, heptanol, octanol, carbenoxolone (positive, a documented innexin/pannexin blocker). For each ligand: mean over seeds of the top-pose DiffDock confidence, and fraction of all poses whose centroid lies within 8 A of the channel axis inside the transmembrane span. Supports: octanol confidence exceeds hexanol's by more than 2 x the larger across-seed SD AND octanol's in-pore fraction exceeds hexanol's by >= 0.25, with carbenoxolone ranking above ethanol on confidence.
tests.fail: Pre-registered. Refutes: hexanol confidence >= octanol's and hexanol in-pore fraction >= octanol's. Inconclusive (reason 'not-operationalizable'): carbenoxolone does not outrank ethanol, the hexanol/octanol confidence difference is within 2 x the across-seed SD, or the hemichannel model's ipTM < 0.50. Anything else is mixed.
tests.interpretation: Tests only the premise that octanol and hexanol differ in gap-junction engagement; the claim's phenotype (no altered head shapes after hexanol) needs new planarian experiments. Alkanol block of gap junctions is thought to act partly through the membrane rather than a defined binding site, and DiffDock confidence is a pose-quality score, not an affinity, so an inconclusive result is a likely and legitimate outcome. Schmidtea mediterranea substitutes for Girardia dorotocephala (both Tricladida; no Girardia innexin sequences are public).

tests.label: Self-assembly emerges from cells sharing a common model of organismal form
tests.hypothesis: In the paper's eight-cell active-inference model, cells that start identical, co-located and undifferentiated, and that share one generative model of the target form, end a 32-step free-energy descent near the target head-body-tail configuration with the correct cell types, while ensemble free energy falls.
tests.pass: Pre-registered: over 20 random seeds (initial expectations drawn with log precision -4, as in the paper), in at least 16 runs (80%) after 32 time steps (a) the RMS distance between final cell positions and target positions under the best one-to-one assignment is below 0.5 x the smallest distance between two target positions, and (b) at least 7 of 8 cells have their most probable identity (softmax of hidden states) belonging to the cell type encoded at their assigned target location; and in every passing run ensemble free energy at step 32 is below its value at step 1.
tests.fail: Pre-registered: fewer than 10 of 20 runs (50%) meet (a) and (b), or ensemble free energy at step 32 is not below step 1 in the majority of runs. Between 10 and 15 passing runs is pre-registered as 'mixed'.
tests.interpretation: MATLAB is unavailable, so the test uses an independent numpy re-implementation (levin-2015-place-01/morphogenesis.py) of DEM_morphogenesis.m. Re-implemented exactly from the file: the 8-cell target (matrix T for L = 2; four cell types coded by signals 1-4), sensations of position (the exogenous linear gradient), intrinsic signal and extracellular signal (monoexponential decay, k = 1, scaled by the sensitivity ramp 1 - exp(-2t) with t = iY/32 as set by spm_ADEM), softmax identity expectations, model sensory precision exp(3), prior precision exp(-2) on identities, action precision exp(2) with action restricted to each cell's own sensations, and initial action equal to the t = 0 prediction (all cells near the centroid). Not re-implemented: spm_ADEM's generalised filter (embedding order 2, local-linearisation update). Instead each of the 32 bins integrates the gradient flow of the Laplace free energy for one time unit (dt = 1, 200 Euler sub-steps; 400 and 800 sub-steps give identical results to 3 decimals). Free energy is spm_ADEM's -J (E'iS E/2 - logdet(qu.c) - logdet(iS)/2) without generalised-motion terms, so only its changes are comparable to the paper's. The paper says initial expectations had 'a log precision of minus four' (sd = e^2 = 7.4), but the file uses randn(n,n)/8 (log precision about +4.2), which matches the paper's 'small random expectations' and 'undifferentiated'. The rule fixed before any baseline run was to run both and call the claim supported only if both pass, and mixed if they disagree. Assessor note checked: the current SPM file's header comment says 16 cells, but its default target (L = 2) has exactly 8 cells, the paper's head-body-tail form, identical in SPM12 r7679 and current main. SPLIT = 0, so the bisection path is off by default, as noted. 'Self-assemble into that form' means that after the paper's 32 time steps the cells sit within half a target spacing (RMS, best one-to-one assignment) of the target positions, with at least 7/8 cells' most probable identity of the type encoded at their position. The paper itself notes the 32-step result is 'not perfect', which is why 7/8 is allowed.
tests.method: analysis.py fetches DEM_morphogenesis.m (SPM12 and current main) and spm_ADEM.m, parses the target and defaults, and runs 20 seeds of the 32-bin simulation for each initial-expectation spread (randn/8 from the file; sd e^2 from the paper's text). Each run is deterministic, plus a sensitivity copy with process noise. At step 32 it computes the RMS position error under the best of all 8! cell-to-target assignments and the number of correctly typed cells, and compares free energy at steps 1 and 32.

measured.unit: runs of 20 assembled at step 32 (file initialisation randn/8)

caveats: Independent re-implementation, not the published MATLAB solver. spm_ADEM's generalised filtering in generalised coordinates can follow a different path through the same free-energy landscape. Nothing was run in MATLAB or Octave.

After seeing the deterministic results, a disclosed sensitivity condition added the SPM generative process's sensory noise (precision exp(16)), which the pre-registered re-implementation omits. It did not change any count by more than one run.
Seeds are numpy default_rng(0..19). The paper reports one run with MATLAB rng('default'), which cannot be matched outside MATLAB.
Cell types use the file's encoding (T values 2, 1, 4, 3 from left to right along the body axis). The paper's head/body/tail labels map onto these four signal codes.

Under the file's initialisation (randn/8) the claim reproduces clearly: 19/20 runs assemble, with median RMS 0.29 against a threshold of 0.5, a median of 8/8 correct types, and free energy falling in every run. Under the paper's literal 'log precision -4' (initial identities already nearly one-hot and random), 14/20 assemble, which falls in the pre-registered mixed band. The mixed verdict comes from that initialisation discrepancy and is not evidence against self-assembly in the model.
This is a proof-of-principle claim about a model. Reproducing it says nothing about whether real cells minimise variational free energy.

tests.label: Free energy is minimized only when every cell occupies a unique inferred place
tests.hypothesis: In the paper's eight-cell active-inference model, free-energy descent run to a steady state reaches the target form (every cell at its own distinct target location with the correct identity) from every initial condition tried, and no non-target stationary state has free energy at or below that of the target form.
tests.pass: Pre-registered. A run 'succeeds' if, at its converged state, (a) the RMS distance between cell positions and target positions under the best one-to-one assignment is below 0.5 x the smallest distance between two target positions, (b) all 8 cells have the identity (softmax argmax) of the type encoded at their assigned target, and (c) the smallest distance between any two cells is at least 0.5 x the smallest target spacing (no two cells share a place). Four families of 50 seeds each (n = 200): F1 initial identity expectations randn/8 with cells co-located (the SPM file's start); F2 initial expectations with sd = e^2 (the paper's literal 'log precision -4'), cells co-located; F3 every cell's identity expectation set to the same single type (v = +4 on one type, 0 elsewhere), cells co-located; F4 cells started at independent uniform random positions in the target bounding box scaled by 1.5, with random identities (randn/8). F1 and F2 are the primary families (the two readings of the paper's start); F3 and F4 are stress families. Supports: 50/50 successes in F1 and in F2, at least 95% successes (48/50) in each of F3 and F4, and no converged non-target stationary state with F <= F_ref + 1.0 nat in any family, where F_ref is the median free energy over all successful runs.
tests.fail: Pre-registered. Refutes: fewer than 25 of 50 successes in F1 or in F2, or at least one converged non-target stationary state with F <= F_ref + 1.0 nat in F1 or F2 (a competing or deeper minimum, which falsifies the 'only' clause), or at least 10% of runs in F1 or F2 ending in a converged non-target stationary state (a reproducible non-target attractor falsifies 'guarantees'). Mixed: every other outcome, including 25-49 successes in F1/F2, 100% in F1 and F2 but fewer than 48/50 in F3 or F4, or a competing minimum only in F3 or F4. Inconclusive (reason 'other'): more than 10% of all runs fail to reach a stationary state within the maximum horizon, or the re-implementation does not reproduce the sibling test levin-2015-place-01 at 32 steps for F1 (fewer than 16 of the first 20 F1 seeds assembled by the pre-registered place-01 criterion), which would mean the model is not faithfully re-implemented.
tests.interpretation: 'The minimum of variational free energy is reached only when every cell is at a unique location and has correctly inferred its place' is read as: every stationary state of the free-energy flow that is a minimum is the target form up to relabelling of cells (cells share one model and are exchangeable, so which cell takes which place is arbitrary; 'unique' means no two cells share a place). 'So free-energy minimization guarantees convergence to the target form' is read as the universal statement that descent reaches that state from any initial condition within the model's scope, tested by sampling four families of starts rather than proven. A finite sample can refute the universal claim but cannot prove it, so 'supports' means 'no counterexample found in 200 runs', and the claim's mathematical form is not established by this test. The 'correctly inferred' requirement is 8/8 correct identities (stricter than the 7/8 allowed in place-01, because this claim says every cell). The exogenous gradient is kept on; its ablation belongs to levin-2015-place-09. The model's prior precision on identities and the log-determinant term mean the free-energy minimum need not coincide exactly with zero prediction error, so success is defined by the tolerances in pass_criterion, not by exact equality.

tests.label: Simulated cells resolve fate ambiguity using context set by other ambiguous cells
tests.hypothesis: In the paper's eight-cell active-inference model started from identical co-located undifferentiated cells, migration toward target locations happens first and fast, differentiation into head/body/tail types follows at around the eighth time step, ensemble free energy falls as identities resolve, and identities end resolved even though each cell's identity depends on signals from other equally ambiguous cells.
tests.pass: Pre-registered, over 20 random seeds (initial expectations with log precision -4), 32 steps: define migration time t_m as the first step at which the mean distance of cells to their best-assigned target positions falls below 50% of its value at step 0, and differentiation time t_d as the first step at which at least 6 of 8 cells have a most-probable identity of the type encoded at their assigned target and mean max identity probability exceeds 0.5. The claim is supported if, in at least 16 of 20 runs: t_m < t_d; t_d lies in [4, 16] (within a factor of 2 of the reported eighth step); ensemble free energy at step 32 is below step 1; and at step 32 mean max identity probability exceeds 0.5 with at least 7/8 cells correctly typed.
tests.fail: Pre-registered: in fewer than 10 of 20 runs the conditions hold, or in the majority of runs differentiation precedes or coincides with migration (t_d <= t_m), or the median t_d is outside [2, 24] or never reached. Between 10 and 15 qualifying runs is 'mixed'.
tests.interpretation: MATLAB is unavailable, so the test uses an independent numpy re-implementation (levin-2015-place-01/morphogenesis.py) of DEM_morphogenesis.m. Re-implemented exactly from the file: the 8-cell target (matrix T for L = 2; four cell types coded by signals 1-4), sensations of position (the exogenous linear gradient), intrinsic signal and extracellular signal (monoexponential decay, k = 1, scaled by the sensitivity ramp 1 - exp(-2t) with t = iY/32 as set by spm_ADEM), softmax identity expectations, model sensory precision exp(3), prior precision exp(-2) on identities, action precision exp(2) with action restricted to each cell's own sensations, and initial action equal to the t = 0 prediction (all cells near the centroid). Not re-implemented: spm_ADEM's generalised filter (embedding order 2, local-linearisation update). Instead each of the 32 bins integrates the gradient flow of the Laplace free energy for one time unit (dt = 1, 200 Euler sub-steps; 400 and 800 sub-steps give identical results to 3 decimals). Free energy is spm_ADEM's -J (E'iS E/2 - logdet(qu.c) - logdet(iS)/2) without generalised-motion terms, so only its changes are comparable to the paper's. The paper says initial expectations had 'a log precision of minus four' (sd = e^2 = 7.4), but the file uses randn(n,n)/8 (log precision about +4.2), which matches the paper's 'small random expectations' and 'undifferentiated'. The rule fixed before any baseline run was to run both and call the claim supported only if both pass, and mixed if they disagree. Assessor note checked: the current SPM file's header comment says 16 cells, but its default target (L = 2) has exactly 8 cells, the paper's head-body-tail form, identical in SPM12 r7679 and current main. SPLIT = 0, so the bisection path is off by default, as noted. 'Migrate rapidly' is the step t_m at which mean distance to the best-assigned targets has halved. 'Differentiate at about the eighth step' is the step t_d at which at least 6/8 cells are correctly typed and mean max identity probability exceeds 0.5, accepted in [4, 16]. 'Resolve ambiguity' means that at step 32 mean max identity probability exceeds 0.5 with at least 7/8 cells correctly typed. Context dependence is built into the model, since each cell senses only other cells' signals and the exogenous gradient.
tests.method: analysis.py runs the same 20-seed, 32-bin simulations as levin-2015-place-01 for both initial-expectation spreads, deterministic plus a process-noise copy. For each run it records t_m, t_d, the free-energy trajectory and step-32 identity resolution, and counts runs meeting all pre-registered conditions.

measured.unit: median differentiation step (file initialisation randn/8)
measured.uncertainty: range 9-14 over 20 seeds

caveats: Independent re-implementation, not the published MATLAB solver. spm_ADEM's generalised filtering in generalised coordinates can follow a different path through the same free-energy landscape. Nothing was run in MATLAB or Octave.

After seeing the deterministic results, a disclosed sensitivity condition added the SPM generative process's sensory noise (precision exp(16)), which the pre-registered re-implementation omits. It did not change any count by more than one run.
Seeds are numpy default_rng(0..19). The paper reports one run with MATLAB rng('default'), which cannot be matched outside MATLAB.
Cell types use the file's encoding (T values 2, 1, 4, 3 from left to right along the body axis). The paper's head/body/tail labels map onto these four signal codes.

Under the file's initialisation the reported sequence reproduces closely in 19/20 runs: migration halves the distance by step 4 (median), differentiation follows at median step 10 (range 9-14), free energy peaks at step 2 and then falls (the paper notes an initial increase), and identities resolve. Under the paper's literal 'log precision -4', 0/20 runs qualify: cells begin with random near-one-hot identities, so median 'differentiation' is step 6.5, before migration (median t_m 17, and in some runs distance never halves). That is the opposite order, and it drives the mixed verdict. The literal reading contradicts the paper's own description of the start as 'undifferentiated'.

tests.label: Bisected simulated embryos regenerate the full target form
tests.hypothesis: In the paper's eight-cell active-inference model, if morphogenesis is run for 8 steps, the embryo is cut into a head half and a tail half, each half's cells are replicated (keeping location and partial differentiation) and each half is integrated separately for 32 more steps, then both halves regenerate the full head-body-tail target, after a transient dedifferentiation.
tests.pass: Pre-registered, over 20 random seeds: after the split and 32 further steps, both halves meet the assembly criterion of levin-2015-place-01 (RMS position error under best one-to-one assignment < 0.5 x smallest target spacing, and >= 7/8 cells correctly typed) in at least 16 of 20 runs; and dedifferentiation is seen, i.e. in the majority of runs, for at least one half, mean max identity probability falls below its value at the split during the first 8 post-split steps.
tests.fail: Pre-registered: fewer than 10 of 20 runs have both halves meeting the assembly criterion. Between 10 and 15 is 'mixed'; full regeneration without any measured dedifferentiation dip is reported as supporting the regeneration part and not the dedifferentiation part ('mixed' if the dip criterion fails).
tests.interpretation: MATLAB is unavailable, so the test uses an independent numpy re-implementation (levin-2015-place-01/morphogenesis.py) of DEM_morphogenesis.m. Re-implemented exactly from the file: the 8-cell target (matrix T for L = 2; four cell types coded by signals 1-4), sensations of position (the exogenous linear gradient), intrinsic signal and extracellular signal (monoexponential decay, k = 1, scaled by the sensitivity ramp 1 - exp(-2t) with t = iY/32 as set by spm_ADEM), softmax identity expectations, model sensory precision exp(3), prior precision exp(-2) on identities, action precision exp(2) with action restricted to each cell's own sensations, and initial action equal to the t = 0 prediction (all cells near the centroid). Not re-implemented: spm_ADEM's generalised filter (embedding order 2, local-linearisation update). Instead each of the 32 bins integrates the gradient flow of the Laplace free energy for one time unit (dt = 1, 200 Euler sub-steps; 400 and 800 sub-steps give identical results to 3 decimals). Free energy is spm_ADEM's -J (E'iS E/2 - logdet(qu.c) - logdet(iS)/2) without generalised-motion terms, so only its changes are comparable to the paper's. The paper says initial expectations had 'a log precision of minus four' (sd = e^2 = 7.4), but the file uses randn(n,n)/8 (log precision about +4.2), which matches the paper's 'small random expectations' and 'undifferentiated'. The rule fixed before any baseline run was to run both and call the claim supported only if both pass, and mixed if they disagree. Assessor note checked: the current SPM file's header comment says 16 cells, but its default target (L = 2) has exactly 8 cells, the paper's head-body-tail form, identical in SPM12 r7679 and current main. SPLIT = 0, so the bisection path is off by default, as noted. The bisection follows the SPLIT branch of the file: at step 8, sort cells by actual position on the body axis and keep the 4 with largest x (upper, the tail-side cells, which must regenerate a head) or smallest x (lower, the head-side cells). Duplicate their identity expectations, positions and signals, add randn/512 jitter to action, and call the 32-bin solver again from those states. As in the file, the sensitivity ramp restarts at t = 1/32. 'Regenerates the complete target' uses the levin-2015-place-01 assembly criterion. 'Slight dedifferentiation' means mean max identity probability dips below its value at the split during the first 8 post-split steps.
tests.method: analysis.py runs 20 seeds per initial-expectation spread, deterministic plus a process-noise copy. Each run goes 8 steps, is split into upper and lower halves, each half's cells are duplicated, and each half runs 32 further steps. It scores whether both halves reach the target (RMS < 0.5 under the best assignment and at least 7/8 correct types), whether identity certainty dips after the cut, and the final separation of duplicated pairs.

measured.unit: runs of 20 in which both halves regenerated the full target (file initialisation randn/8)

caveats: Independent re-implementation, not the published MATLAB solver. spm_ADEM's generalised filtering in generalised coordinates can follow a different path through the same free-energy landscape. Nothing was run in MATLAB or Octave.

After seeing the deterministic results, a disclosed sensitivity condition added the SPM generative process's sensory noise (precision exp(16)), which the pre-registered re-implementation omits. It did not change any count by more than one run.
Seeds are numpy default_rng(0..19). The paper reports one run with MATLAB rng('default'), which cannot be matched outside MATLAB.
Cell types use the file's encoding (T values 2, 1, 4, 3 from left to right along the body axis). The paper's head/body/tail labels map onto these four signal codes.

Dedifferentiation reproduces in every run (20/20 under both initialisations), but full regeneration of both halves does not: 3/20 runs with the file's initialisation and 6/20 with the paper's (7/20 with process noise). Each half regenerates on its own in only 5-11 of 20 runs. Failing halves end with separated cells (duplicate pairs 0.6-0.8 apart) in a wrong arrangement, typically with 6/8 correct types and RMS error about 0.6-0.8. That is a mis-assembled form, not a collapse.

The paper reports a single bisection run that regenerates. This result says that outcome is not robust across seeds in a faithful re-implementation of the model. It does not show that the published MATLAB run is wrong. spm_ADEM's generalised filter could make regeneration more reliable than gradient flow does, so the refutation is limited to the model under gradient-descent integration, hence the low confidence.
The planarian and regulative-embryo analogy in the claim's scope is not tested.

tests.label: Embryonic nicotine exposure causes major brain malformations in Xenopus
tests.hypothesis: In published embryo-level counts, Xenopus laevis embryos exposed to 0.1 mg/mL nicotine (stages 10-35) show major brain morphology defects at stage 45 at a much higher rate (about 55%) than untreated controls (about 6%).
tests.pass: Pre-registered: from published counts (affected / scored tadpoles) for nicotine-exposed and control embryos under the claim's protocol, (a) the incidence of major brain defects is >= 40% with nicotine and <= 15% in controls, and (b) the difference is significant by a two-sided Fisher exact test at p < 0.001. If only percentages and group sizes are published, counts are reconstructed as round(percentage x n) and this is stated.
tests.fail: Pre-registered: nicotine incidence minus control incidence < 10 percentage points, or Fisher p >= 0.05. Outcomes in between (significant but outside the magnitude bands in (a)) are pre-registered as 'mixed'. If no counts or group sizes for both groups can be obtained from a public source, the verdict is 'inconclusive' (data-unavailable).
tests.interpretation: 'Major brain morphology defects' follows the paper's scoring (absent nostrils, forebrain or midbrain, or misformed hindbrain at stage 45). The test checks that the published counts support the stated incidence contrast; with only the source paper's data available it is an audit of the reported numbers, not an independent replication, and is labelled as such. Mortality differences, clutch structure and blinding cannot be assessed from aggregate counts. The claim's mechanistic context (nicotine acting through disruption of the brain bioelectric prepattern) is not tested.
tests.method: analysis.py downloads the Pai et al. 2018 full text and the Tung et al. 2024 Source Data, checks that the quoted incidence sentences and the figure-legend group sizes occur verbatim in the full text, and reconstructs counts as round(percentage x 153), 153 = 3 experiments x 51 embryos being the smallest total consistent with 'N > 50 embryos per treatment group for each of those experiments'. It runs a two-sided Fisher exact test for Fig. 1d (primary) and Fig. 5f (repeat within the paper) and reports the smallest per-group N at which p < 0.001 would still hold. Tung et al. per-replicate nicotine defect percentages by group size are summarized as context.

measured.unit: percent of stage-45 tadpoles with major brain defects, nicotine vs control (Pai et al. 2018 Fig. 1d, as reported)
measured.uncertainty: counts reconstructed at the legend's lower bound N = 153 per group; Fisher p = 3.62e-22

caveats: Not independent: the only admissible counts are the source paper's own, and only as rounded percentages ('~55%', '~6%') with a lower bound on group size. The test confirms that the reported numbers, taken at face value, meet the pre-registered contrast with a wide margin (p < 0.001 would hold with as few as 21 embryos per group); it cannot check scoring, blinding or mortality.

Fisher's test treats embryos as independent. The paper's own analysis used n = 3 experiments (t-test, p < 0.01), and clutch effects could make the embryo-level p far too small; the effect size (about nine-fold) is the more robust quantity.
Within the paper the contrast repeats (Fig. 5f: ~60% vs ~7%), but that is the same lab and protocol.

Context from a later Levin-lab study (Tung et al. 2024, same dose, stages 11-35): the nicotine-induced brain-defect rate depends strongly on how many embryos are reared together, from 96.7% in groups of 10 to 46.9% at 50, 22% at 100 and 10.1% at 125. Nicotine reliably causes brain malformations, but 'about 55%' is a property of the rearing conditions, not a fixed teratogenic rate. Those values are normalized to untreated controls and so do not test the 6% control rate.
Pai et al. state that individual-level data are available from the corresponding author on request; no embryo-level table is deposited, and the supplementary PDF contains only model notes.
