tests.label: HCN2 modelled as a voltage-controlled switch that amplifies small Vmem gradients
tests.hypothesis: In a coupled-cell bioelectric model of the anterior stage-15 Xenopus neurula built with the paper's stated ingredients (Table 1 concentrations, 0.1x MMR medium, three regions whose K+/Cl- leak differences give a hyperpolarized neural tube near -50 mV and lateral neural folds/ectoderm near -5 mV, Kir channels, voltage-sensitive gap junctions) and BETSE's HCN2 kinetic model (V1/2 = -99 mV shifted +20 mV by cAMP, Na+:K+ permeability 0.2), adding homogeneously expressed HCN2 opens it preferentially in the hyperpolarized tube, drives tube cells further negative, and leaves the depolarized lateral regions essentially unchanged, i.e. it amplifies the existing Vmem gradient rather than shifting all regions uniformly.
tests.pass: Pre-registered, evaluated at the primary HCN2 expression level (the paper's/BETSE's stated HCN2 maximum permeability if recoverable from Table 1, the Supplementary Note or a published BETSE config; otherwise the BETSE default for its HCN2 channel class) in the three-region coupled sheet calibrated so the HCN2-free control gives tube Vmem within -50 +/- 10 mV and lateral Vmem within -5 +/- 5 mV: ALL of (a) the GHK reversal potential of HCN2 current under Table 1 cytosol and 0.1x MMR is more negative than the control tube Vmem; (b) tube Vmem with HCN2 minus control tube Vmem <= -15 mV; (c) the largest absolute change in mean Vmem of either lateral region <= 5 mV; (d) the lateral-minus-tube Vmem difference increases by >= 15 mV; (e) steady-state HCN2 open probability in the tube is >= 5 times that in the ectoderm. Secondary (switch/amplification): in uncoupled single cells whose control Vmem is swept from about -70 to 0 mV by varying K+ leak, the HCN2-induced shift is >= 15 mV in magnitude for some cells with control Vmem <= -40 mV and <= 5 mV for all cells with control Vmem >= -15 mV, and the expression range (log sweep 0.01x to 100x the primary level) over which (b)-(d) all hold spans at least one decade.
tests.fail: Pre-registered: any of (i) HCN2 reversal potential more positive than the control tube Vmem (opening would depolarize the tube); (ii) tube shift > -5 mV at the primary expression level (no amplification); (iii) lateral shift magnitude >= half the tube shift magnitude at the primary level (near-uniform shift, not switch-like); (iv) no expression level in the 0.01x-100x sweep satisfies (b)-(d). Outcomes meeting neither the pass nor the fail criterion are pre-registered as 'mixed'. If the control calibration (tube -50 +/- 10, lateral -5 +/- 5 mV) cannot be achieved with Table 1 concentrations and the stated channel set, verdict is 'inconclusive' with reason 'other'.

tests.label: Native HCN2 activity is not required for normal brain patterning
tests.hypothesis: The GYG->AAA mouse HCN2 construct used in the paper can still co-assemble with wild-type HCN2 subunits (the premise that makes it dominant-negative), so that a construct which fails to disrupt patterning can be read as evidence that native HCN2 activity is not required.
tests.pass: Pre-registered. Model: mouse HCN2 (UniProt O88703) residues 131-520 (assembly region, S1-S6 and C-linker). AlphaFold3 on the Nebius Scientific AI Platform predicts (a) a wild-type homotetramer, (b) a 1 AAA : 3 WT heterotetramer and (c) an AAA homotetramer. stab-ddG on the wild-type tetramer predicts the change in binding energy between chain A and chains B+C+D for G402A/Y403A/G404A on chain A. Supports the premise if ALL of: WT ipTM >= 0.60; heterotetramer ipTM >= WT ipTM - 0.10; AAA binding ddG <= 1.0 kcal/mol; and the sensitivity control (chain-A residue with the most inter-subunit heavy-atom contacts within 4 A, mutated to Arg) gives ddG >= 2.0 kcal/mol.
tests.fail: Pre-registered. Refutes the premise if the sensitivity control passes and either AAA ddG >= 2.0 kcal/mol or heterotetramer ipTM < WT ipTM - 0.20. Inconclusive (reason 'other') if WT ipTM < 0.60 or the sensitivity control gives ddG < 2.0 kcal/mol (assay cannot detect a disrupted interface). Anything else is mixed.
tests.interpretation: This tests a premise of the claim, not the claim's phenotype: whether the reagent can do what 'dominant-negative' requires (co-assemble and poison the tetramer). That native HCN2 activity is not needed for brain patterning (levin-2018-hcn2-16), and that rescue needs conductance (levin-2018-hcn2-12), both rest on it. Non-conduction itself is not tested; computational structure predictors are known to be insensitive to pore point mutations, and the paper reports voltage-clamp data for that (Supplementary Fig. 2A).

tests.label: Animal senses use the same ion channel mechanisms found in bacteria
tests.hypothesis: For each of the four senses named (touch, taste, temperature, hearing), at least one ion channel that transduces that sense in animals has a predicted structure containing the fold of a known bacterial ion channel, as measured by TM-score, clearly above the score a non-channel membrane protein reaches against the same bacterial channel.
tests.pass: Pre-registered. Structures for every protein are predicted with ESMFold2 on the Nebius Scientific AI Platform (single-sequence mode, seed 0) and aligned pairwise with TM-align (tmtools); the TM-score is normalised by the length of the bacterial chain. A sense is 'shared' if some channel listed for it reaches TM >= 0.50 against some bacterial channel AND that score exceeds the GLUT1 negative control's score against the same bacterial channel by >= 0.10. Supports: all four senses shared, with both controls behaving (positive control KCNA2 vs KcsA TM >= 0.50; negative controls myoglobin and GLUT1 below 0.50 against every bacterial channel).
tests.fail: Pre-registered. Refutes: no sense is shared. Mixed: one to three senses shared. Inconclusive (reason 'other'): the positive control scores below 0.50, either negative control reaches 0.50 against any bacterial channel, or every channel listed for a sense has mean pLDDT < 50 (that sense is then reported as undetermined and the verdict is at most mixed).
tests.interpretation: 'The exact same ion channel mechanisms' is read as shared structural ancestry of the channel protein, the strongest sense in which a mechanism can be 'the same' across 3+ billion years; a shared biophysical principle without homology (e.g. any force-gated pore) would not count. Senses are mapped to the channels that transduce them in mammals: touch to PIEZO2; temperature to TRPV1 (heat) and TRPM8 (cold); taste to OTOP1 (sour), ENaC alpha/SCNN1A (salty) and TRPM5 (sweet, bitter and umami downstream of GPCRs); hearing to TMC1. Monomers are compared because the pore-forming fold lives in a single subunit for all of these families.

tests.label: Selection for locomotion under random actuation evolved derandomizing shapes
tests.hypothesis: In a voxel soft-body simulation where each contractile voxel's phase offset is random and fixed per clade (so selection can only change which voxels exist and which are contractile), selection for net displacement yields designs that move much farther than random designs under the same random actuation, and the gain depends on the evolved arrangement of passive and contractile voxels rather than on the particular phases.
tests.pass: Pre-registered, on the second-pass setting (water: reduced gravity plus drag; random fixed phases), over the independent evolutionary trials analysed: (a) the median ratio of final-champion net displacement to the mean displacement of random designs is >= 2, and >= 80% of champions exceed the 95th percentile of random designs; (b) shuffling which of the champion's voxels are contractile (same shape, same number of contractile voxels, same phase field, 20 shuffles) reduces displacement: median over champions of (median shuffled displacement / champion displacement) <= 0.7; (c) re-evaluating each champion's body under fresh random phase fields (20 draws) gives a median displacement above the 95th percentile of random designs for >= 70% of champions. Supports if (a), (b) and (c) all hold.
tests.fail: Pre-registered: refutes if (a) fails badly (median champion/random ratio <= 1.2, or < 50% of champions above the random 95th percentile), or if (b) shows no dependence on material layout (median shuffled/champion ratio >= 0.95) and (c) fails (champions under fresh phases at or below the random-design median for >= 50% of champions). Any other outcome is 'mixed'. If neither published outputs nor a working simulator (original or the simplified re-implementation below) can be run, verdict is inconclusive (data-unavailable or not-operationalizable).

tests.label: Adding hydrodynamics and random actuation made simulated gaits match living ones
tests.hypothesis: Designs evolved for locomotion on simulated land with evolvable (finely tuned) actuation phases spend a large fraction of their evaluation airborne, whereas designs evolved with first-order hydrodynamics (reduced gravity plus surface drag) and random clade-fixed phase offsets stay in contact with the ground almost all the time, as living deciliated organisms do (93.3% vs 52.7% ground contact in the paper).
tests.pass: Pre-registered. Tier A (published outputs or original simulator): mean ground-contact fraction of second-pass designs within 5 percentage points of 93.3% and of first-pass designs within 5 points of 52.7%, and second minus first >= 20 points. Tier B (simplified re-implementation, numbers not expected to match): mean contact fraction of second-pass champions >= 85% and second minus first >= 20 percentage points, with a permutation test p < 0.05 over trials. Contact at a time step = lowest node within 0.05 voxel lengths of the ground plane; fraction taken over the evaluation period.
tests.fail: Pre-registered: refutes if second-pass contact fraction <= first-pass + 5 points (no improvement), or (Tier A) if either published mean differs from the paper's figure by > 15 points. Other outcomes are 'mixed'. If neither published outputs nor a runnable simulator is available, verdict inconclusive (data-unavailable).

tests.label: Genes for morphogenesis and for learning and memory should overlap widely
tests.hypothesis: Among mouse genes with experimental Gene Ontology biological-process annotations, genes annotated to learning or memory are over-represented among genes annotated to anatomical structure morphogenesis, even after removing ion channels, gap-junction channels and neurotransmission genes, and this overlap is larger than the overlap of morphogenesis with other biological-process terms of similar size.
tests.pass: Pre-registered: after exclusions, (a) the one-sided Fisher exact test of overlap between the learning-or-memory set (GO:0007611 and is_a/part_of descendants) and the morphogenesis set (GO:0009653 and descendants) gives odds ratio > 1.5 and p < 0.001; (b) the Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio stratified by deciles of each gene's number of experimental BP annotations is > 1.5; (c) the unstratified odds ratio is above the 75th percentile of odds ratios between the morphogenesis set and every control BP term whose post-exclusion gene count is within a factor of 1.5 of the learning-or-memory set's and which is neither an ancestor nor a descendant of GO:0007611 or GO:0009653.
tests.fail: Pre-registered: unstratified odds ratio <= 1.2 or p >= 0.05, or Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio <= 1.2, or the odds ratio at or below the median of the size-matched control terms. Outcomes meeting neither criterion are pre-registered as 'mixed' (overlap present but not specific, or explained by annotation depth).
tests.interpretation: TAME's prediction is phrased across animals; the test uses the mouse because MGI curation gives the deepest experimental annotation of both developmental and behavioural phenotypes in a single species. 'Genes involved in morphogenesis' is GO:0009653 anatomical structure morphogenesis and 'memory and learning categories' is GO:0007611 learning or memory, each with is_a and part_of descendants. Only experimental evidence codes (EXP, IDA, IPI, IMP, IGI, IEP, HTP, HDA, HMP, HGI, HEP) are used, so electronic or sequence-similarity annotations cannot create the overlap. The universe is every gene with at least one such BP annotation, after removing NOT-qualified lines. 'Beyond the known shared ion channels, connexins and neurotransmitter machinery' is implemented by excluding from the universe every gene annotated (any evidence) to GO:0005216 ion channel activity, GO:0005243 gap junction channel activity, GO:0005921 gap junction, GO:0007268 chemical synaptic transmission, GO:0001505 regulation of neurotransmitter levels or GO:0030594 neurotransmitter receptor activity, with descendants. Only the first part of the claim is tested; its second part (memory genes appearing in cancer, regeneration and embryogenesis screens) is out of scope here.
tests.method: fetch.py downloads go-basic.obo and the MGI GAF. analysis.py drops NOT-qualified and obsolete-term lines, builds each gene's set of experimental BP terms and their is_a/part_of ancestors, removes 612 genes annotated to ion channel, gap junction or neurotransmission terms, and tests overlap of GO:0007611 and GO:0009653 in the remaining 10,243 genes with a one-sided Fisher exact test. Annotation depth is controlled by a Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio over ten equal-sized strata of genes ranked by their number of distinct experimental BP terms. Specificity is the percentile of the odds ratio among the 327 BP terms of 128-286 genes that are neither ancestors nor descendants of either term.

measured.unit: odds ratio, learning-or-memory vs anatomical-structure-morphogenesis gene sets (mouse, experimental BP annotations, channel/synaptic genes excluded)
measured.uncertainty: one-sided Fisher exact p = 1.140e-09

caveats: The crude overlap is real: 69 genes against 34 expected (odds ratio 2.66, p = 1.1e-9), and removing channel, gap-junction and neurotransmission genes barely changes it (2.64 before exclusion). It does not survive control for annotation depth: learning-or-memory genes sit almost entirely in the most-annotated strata, and within the top decile (13-167 BP terms) 43 of 63 of them (68%) are morphogenesis genes against 621 of 961 other genes (65%). The pre-registered fail rule is met by the Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio (0.94 <= 1.2). The control comparison (64.5th percentile) fails pass criterion (c) but does not by itself meet the fail rule, since 2.66 is above the control median of 1.87.

Size-matched control terms include developmental processes adjacent to morphogenesis (axon, limb, cardiac chamber, neural tube development) with very high odds ratios, which raises the 75th-percentile bar; the depth-stratified result does not depend on this choice.

GO annotations reflect what has been studied: genes are annotated to learning or memory largely because they were knocked out and tested behaviourally, which happens mostly to genes already well studied in development. Annotation-depth stratification addresses this only approximately.
Mouse only and experimental evidence only. TAME frames the prediction across animals; other species or inclusion of inferred annotations could differ.
Only the first half of the claim is tested. Whether memory genes appear in cancer, regeneration and embryogenesis screens is not addressed.
The GO release is 'current' at retrieval time and is not versioned in the URL; re-running later will fetch a newer release, so exact numbers will drift. The SHA-256 above identifies the files used.

tests.label: Genes for morphogenesis and for learning and memory should overlap widely
tests.hypothesis: Second half of the claim: mouse learning-or-memory genes are over-represented among genes whose mutants show cancer, regeneration or embryogenesis phenotypes, beyond what their depth of phenotyping explains.
tests.pass: Pre-registered: for each of the three outcome categories (cancer, regeneration, embryogenesis), the Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio of the learning-or-memory set versus the outcome set, stratified by deciles of each gene's number of distinct MP phenotype terms, is > 1.5 with one-sided Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel p < 0.001. The claim is supported if all three pass.
tests.fail: Pre-registered: the claim is refuted if the stratified odds ratio is <= 1.2 or p >= 0.05 in at least two of the three categories. Any other outcome (for example one or two categories pass) is 'mixed'. Unstratified odds ratios and raw counts ('memory genes appear at all') are reported but are not decisive, because almost any well-studied gene set 'appears' in large phenotype catalogues.
tests.interpretation: 'Genetic studies of cancer, regeneration and embryogenesis' are operationalised as mouse mutant phenotypes curated by MGI (MGI_GenePheno.rpt: genotypes with a mutation in one marker), mapped to genes by MGI marker ID. Outcome sets, each with all MP is_a descendants: cancer = MP:0002006 neoplasm; embryogenesis = MP:0001672 abnormal embryo development or MP:0008762 embryonic lethality; regeneration = every MP term whose label contains 'regenerat' (MP has no single regeneration parent; this includes e.g. MP:0002658 abnormal liver regeneration, MP:0000750 abnormal muscle regeneration, MP:0004858 abnormal nervous system regeneration). 'Memory genes' are defined as in the first-half test (test-data/claim-tests/levin-papers/levin-2022-tame-19): GO:0007611 learning or memory and descendants, experimental evidence codes only, so the memory set is defined independently of the MP outcome annotations. The universe is genes with at least one MP annotation in MGI_GenePheno.rpt and at least one experimental GO BP annotation. The claim's second half has no 'beyond ion channels' qualifier, so the primary analysis does not exclude channel or synaptic genes; the first-half exclusion is repeated as a secondary analysis. Secondary analyses also report the same test with the memory set defined genetically by MP:0002063 abnormal learning/memory/conditioning, and stratified by GO experimental BP depth instead of MP depth. Secondary analyses do not change the verdict.
tests.method: fetch.py downloads the four files; analysis.py reuses the first-half test's GO parsing and memory-set definition. The universe is the 9,325 genes with both an MP annotation in MGI_GenePheno.rpt and an experimental GO BP annotation. For each outcome set (MP:0002006 neoplasm; MP:0001672 or MP:0008762 for embryogenesis; the 33 MP terms whose label contains 'regenerat'), it computes the unstratified odds ratio and Fisher test, and the Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio with a one-sided continuity-corrected CMH test over deciles of genes ranked by number of distinct MP terms. Secondary runs exclude channel/synaptic genes, stratify by GO depth instead, or define memory genes by MP:0002063.

measured.unit: Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio (phenotyping-depth deciles), GO learning-or-memory genes vs MP embryogenesis phenotype genes; cancer and regeneration in extra
measured.uncertainty: one-sided CMH p = 9.696e-01

caveats: Memory genes do 'appear' in all three kinds of study (15 cancer, 45 embryogenesis and 3 regeneration genes in the primary set), as they would for nearly any gene set this size. The pre-registered test asks whether they appear more than expected; they appear slightly less than expected in all three categories once phenotyping depth is controlled, and no primary or GO-defined secondary analysis reaches significance in the claim's direction.

The one positive signal is secondary: with memory genes defined by mutant phenotype (MP:0002063, 1,248 genes) the regeneration odds ratio is 1.97 (CMH p = 0.007, 21 observed vs 12.5 expected), spread across nervous-system, liver and muscle regeneration terms. It does not meet the pre-registered p < 0.001 and is the kind of result an extension should test properly.

Viability bias: a mouse that dies as an embryo cannot be tested for learning, which would push the embryogenesis overlap down. The effect looks modest here (11.7% of MP-memory genes are also embryonic lethal against 14.6% of all phenotyped genes, presumably through heterozygous and conditional alleles), but it biases the embryogenesis comparison against the claim.

MGI phenotype curation is literature-driven: which phenotypes were looked for depends on each lab's interest, so 'not annotated' is not 'tested and normal'. Depth stratification controls only partly for this. A systematic screen such as IMPC, which runs every knockout through the same pipeline, would be a stronger test for viability, though IMPC barely assays learning or tumours.
Mouse only. TAME's 'genetic studies' could equally mean planarian RNAi regeneration screens, zebrafish fin-regeneration mutants or human cancer driver lists; those are not tested here.
MP has no single regeneration parent term; the regeneration set is the union of 33 label-matched terms and is small (95 genes), so that comparison is underpowered (3 overlapping genes).

tests.label: Higher cellular competency accelerates evolutionary search in a 1D embryo model
tests.hypothesis: In an independent re-implementation of the Shreesha & Levin (2023) artificial-embryogeny genetic algorithm, the best individual's phenotypic fitness (mean over repeats) crosses each fitness threshold sooner the higher the competency level, with competency 400 reaching fitness 1.0 within a few generations and the hardwired population taking far longer.
tests.pass: Pre-registered: with 100 repeats of 250 generations per condition, (a) the generation at which the mean best phenotypic fitness first reaches 1.0 is strictly ordered hardwired > competency 20 > competency 100 > competency 400, and the same weak ordering (>=) holds at every Table 1 threshold (0.65, 0.75, 0.8, 0.9, 0.97, 1.0); (b) competency 400 reaches 1.0 by generation 10 and hardwired does not reach it before generation 100; (c) at generations 2, 10 and 20 each competent population's best phenotypic fitness exceeds hardwired with Welch t-test p < 0.001.
tests.fail: Pre-registered: at the 0.97 or 1.0 threshold some higher competency level is strictly slower than a lower one (including hardwired faster than any competent level), or a competent population is not better than hardwired at generation 10 (p >= 0.05 or lower mean). Outcomes meeting neither the pass nor the fail criterion (ordering holds but the magnitudes in (b) or the significance in (c) are not met) are pre-registered as 'mixed'.
tests.interpretation: This is a simulation-result claim, so the test is replication: re-run the described model and check that the reported dynamics follow from it. Parameters are taken from Supplement S1/S2.1 of the paper (array of 50 cells, values 1-50 drawn with repetition, 100 embryos, top 10% selected on phenotypic fitness, crossover, per-individual point-mutation probability 0.6, competency levels 20/100/400) and unspecified details from the authors' code (github.com/Niwhskal/CellularCompetency, commit 2be29f96): fitness 9^x/9 where x is the normalized non-inversion count; restricted bubble sort that swaps strictly inverted adjacent pairs, visiting positions in a fresh random order each sweep, up to the competency limit; selected parents are kept and children are added by single-point crossover (cut in [11, 50)) until the population is refilled, then every individual is point-mutated with probability 0.6. 'Reaches a threshold' follows the paper's Table 1: the first generation at which the mean over repeats of the best individual's fitness is >= the threshold. The re-implementation is written independently (vectorised numpy) and does not import the authors' code.
tests.method: analysis.py re-implements the model in vectorised numpy without importing the authors' code: per generation it records the best genotypic fitness, develops each embryo by restricted bubble sort, selects the top 10 on phenotypic fitness, refills to 100 by single-point crossover and point-mutates each individual with probability 0.6. Hardwired and competency 20, 100 and 400 populations are each run 100 times for 250 generations from fixed seeds. For each Table 1 threshold it reports the first generation at which the mean best phenotypic fitness reaches it, and runs one-sided Welch t-tests of each competent population against hardwired at generations 2, 10 and 20.

measured.unit: generations for the mean best phenotypic fitness of the competency-400 population to reach 1.0
measured.uncertainty: Monte Carlo; fixed seed, deterministic for a given numpy version

caveats: This is a replication of a simulation, not an empirical test: it shows the reported dynamics follow from the stated model, not that real cellular competency accelerates evolution.

All pre-registered criteria hold: strict ordering at fitness 1.0 (230 > 72 > 33 > 4 generations), weak ordering at every threshold, competency 400 at 1.0 by generation 4, hardwired after generation 100, and every Welch test p < 1e-10.

The re-run is consistently somewhat faster than Table 1 (e.g. competency 20 reaches 1.0 at 72 vs 93, hardwired at 230 vs 250). The authors' plotting code counts hardwired crossings from 0 and competent crossings from 1, and their committed configuration uses 10 repeats rather than the 100 stated in the supplement; either could account for small offsets. The qualitative claim does not depend on them.

'Under 6 generations at competency 400' is reproduced (4); the claim's 'over 200 for hardwired' is reproduced (230), but that number is sensitive to the 1.0 threshold, which requires every one of the 100 repeats to be perfectly sorted in the same generation.

Genotypic fitness plateaus lower the higher the competency (0.97, 0.87 and 0.59 at generation 250 vs 1.0 hardwired), consistent with the companion claim levin-2023-competency-05; that claim is not tested here.

datasets.name: Re-implementation of Shreesha & Levin (2023) Experiment 1, 100 repeats x 250 generations x 4 populations (generated by analysis.py)

tests.label: Cellular competency reduces selective pressure on structural genes
tests.hypothesis: In a re-run of the Shreesha & Levin (2023) Experiment 1 model (fixed competency 20/100/400 vs hardwired, 100 repeats x 250 generations), the best genotypic fitness of each competent population stops rising and stays below the hardwired population's, its spread across repeats grows with competency, while phenotypic fitness stays high.
tests.pass: Pre-registered, with 'best genotypic fitness' = the maximum genotypic (pre-development) fitness in the population each generation, as in the authors' code: (A) at generation 250 each competent population's mean best genotypic fitness is below hardwired, one-sided Welch t-test p < 0.001; (B) plateau: for each competency level, |mean of the mean curve over generations 226-250 minus mean over generations 126-150| < 0.03; (C) the across-repeat standard deviation of best genotypic fitness, averaged over generations 51-250, is strictly ordered competency 20 < 100 < 400; (D) mean best phenotypic fitness at generation 250 >= 0.95 for every competency level. All four -> supports.
tests.fail: Pre-registered: refutes if any competent level's mean best genotypic fitness at generation 250 is >= hardwired, or the generation-51-250 SD at competency 400 is below that at competency 20, or any competent level's genotypic mean curve still rises by more than 0.1 between the 126-150 and 226-250 windows. Any other failure of (A)-(D) -> mixed.
tests.interpretation: Simulation-result claim, tested by replication. 'Genotypic fitness of the best individual' is taken, as in the authors' Exp1 code, as the maximum pre-development fitness in the population each generation. 'Plateaued' is operationalised as < 0.03 change in the repeat-mean curve between generations 126-150 and 226-250; 'wider variance' as the across-repeat SD of best genotypic fitness averaged over generations 51-250; 'high phenotypic fitness' as mean best phenotypic fitness >= 0.95 at generation 250. 'Reduced selective pressure on structural genes' is the authors' interpretation of the lower plateau and is not measured separately.
tests.method: analysis.py imports run() from the levin-2023-competency-04 re-implementation and re-runs hardwired and competency 20, 100 and 400 populations, 100 repeats of 250 generations each, from a new master seed. It compares best genotypic fitness at generation 250 with hardwired by one-sided Welch t-tests, measures the change in the mean genotypic curve between generations 126-150 and 226-250, the across-repeat SD of best genotypic fitness over generations 51-250 per level, and best phenotypic fitness at generation 250.

measured.unit: mean best genotypic fitness at generation 250, competency 400 (hardwired: see extra)
measured.uncertainty: Monte Carlo; fixed seed, deterministic for a given numpy version

caveats: This is a replication of a simulation, not an empirical test: it shows what follows from the stated model, not what real cellular competency does.

All pre-registered criteria hold: genotypic fitness at generation 250 is 0.973, 0.872 and 0.584 at competency 20, 100 and 400 vs 1.000 hardwired (all p < 1e-80); the curves change by < 0.003 between the two windows; across-repeat SD rises 0.0040 < 0.0094 < 0.0211; phenotypic fitness is 1.0 at every level.

How long genotypic fitness tracks hardwired before plateauing depends strongly on competency: the competent mean first falls 0.02 below hardwired at generation 85, 33 and 6 for competency 20, 100 and 400. 'Rose briefly' fits competency 400 best; at competency 20 the genotypic curve follows hardwired for most of the climb.

The companion test levin-2023-competency-04 had already reported generation-250 genotypic means (0.97, 0.87, 0.59) before this test was pre-registered, so the direction of criterion A was known; this run uses independent seeds.

Authors' simulation code for Shreesha & Levin (2023), CellularCompetency

tests.label: Competent embryos take over mixed populations given enough competency or numbers
tests.hypothesis: In a re-implementation of the Shreesha & Levin (2023) mixed-population experiment (200 embryos, hardwired plus a competent minority, selection of the top 10% on phenotypic fitness, 20 generations), the competency needed for competent embryos to dominate falls as their initial share rises (about 75 at 10%, 40 at 20%, 10 at 30%), they do not dominate at 2.5% even at competency 95, and when they dominate they do so within two or three generations.
tests.pass: Pre-registered design: initial competent shares 2.5%, 10%, 20%, 30% (5, 20, 40, 60 of 200) x competency 5, 10, ..., 95 (19 levels) x 50 repeats x 20 generations (generation 1 = initial population, counts taken before selection). 'Dominates' = mean over repeats of the competent share at generation 20 > 0.5. c*(p) = smallest tested competency from which dominance holds at that and every higher tested level (c* = 100 if none). Pass if all of: (P1) c*(10%) > c*(20%) > c*(30%); (P2) |c*(10%) - 75| <= 20, |c*(20%) - 40| <= 20, c*(30%) <= 20; (P3) at 2.5% and competency 95 the mean competent share at generation 20 is <= 0.6; (P4) in every dominating condition at 10/20/30% with competency >= c*, the mean competent share first exceeds 0.5 within 3 rounds of selection (by generation 4).
tests.fail: Pre-registered: refutes if c*(30%) >= c*(10%) (threshold does not fall with share), or |c* - claimed| > 40 for any of 10/20/30%, or at 2.5% competency 95 the mean competent share at generation 20 is > 0.75. Any other failure of P1-P4 -> mixed. A sensitivity run reproducing two quirks of the authors' code (the type label can be overwritten by point mutation and the last structural gene is never mutated) is reported but does not enter the verdict.
tests.interpretation: Simulation-result claim, tested by replication of the mixed-population experiment as the paper describes it: 200 embryos, a competent minority with a fixed competency, competent embryos selected on phenotypic and hardwired on genotypic fitness, top 10% kept, crossover and point mutation, 20 generations. The type label is heritable and goes with the left crossover segment as in the authors' code. 'Dominate' = mean competent share over 50 repeats at generation 20 > 0.5; 'competency needed' = the smallest tested level (5-swap grid) from which dominance holds at all higher levels. The paper reports neither its dominance criterion nor its number of runs ('several'), and its Table 2 was not available to this test. A sensitivity variant reproduces two quirks of the authors' Exp2 code: point mutations are drawn over the label position too (so about 1.2% of embryos per generation get a label that is developed as competent but counted as hardwired), and the last structural gene is never mutated.
tests.method: analysis.py simulates mixed populations of 200 embryos with 5, 20, 40 or 60 competent embryos (2.5, 10, 20, 30%) at competency 5 to 95 in steps of 5, 50 repeats of 20 generations each, for the model as described and for the authors'-code-quirk variant. Each generation it records the competent share before selection. Dominance and the threshold c* are read from the mean share at generation 20, and the takeover time from the first generation at which the mean share exceeds 0.5.

measured.unit: smallest tested competency (5-swap grid, 5-95; 100 = none) from which the mean competent share at generation 20 exceeds 0.5, by initial competent share
measured.uncertainty: Monte Carlo; fixed seed, deterministic for a given numpy version; threshold resolution 5 swaps

caveats: This is a replication of a simulation, not an empirical test: it shows what follows from the stated model, not what real cellular competency does.

In the model as described, the threshold falls with initial share only from 10% to 20% (c* = 35, 15, 15 at 10, 20, 30% vs claimed 75, 40, 10), and at 2.5% competents reach a mean share of 0.94 at competency 95 (c* = 60), so the pre-registered fail rule (2.5% share > 0.75) triggers. At the lowest dominating level the mean share first exceeded 0.5 at generation 5-8 (4-7 rounds of selection), so P4 fails too; well above the threshold it did so at generation 2-3.
The qualitative direction (more competency or a larger initial share makes takeover more likely) is reproduced; what fails is the reported numbers and the 2.5% non-dominance.

The authors'-code-quirk variant comes much closer to the paper: c* = 65, 35, 25 at 10, 20, 30% and a mean share of 0.40 at 2.5% / competency 95 (no level up to 95 dominates). This suggests the published values depend on the label-mutation quirk of the released code, in which mutated competent-developing embryos are counted as hardwired, rather than on the model as described. The verdict follows the pre-registered rule for the model as described.
Dominance is defined here on mean share over 50 repeats; the paper does not say how 'dominate' or 'equal percentages' was judged or how many runs it used, and Table 2 was not consulted.

tests.label: Evolvable competency rises rapidly and plateaus at a high level
tests.hypothesis: In a re-implementation of the Shreesha & Levin (2023) evolvable-competency experiment (competency gene in [1, 500] initialised in [1, 15], 1000 generations), the best individual's competency gene rises rapidly and plateaus around 470, above the competency needed to sort its genome.
tests.pass: Pre-registered design: 30 repeats x 1000 generations, 100 embryos. 'Best individual' (primary) = the individual with the highest genotypic fitness, first in population order on ties, as in the authors' Exp3 code; secondary = the individual ranked first on phenotypic fitness. 'Needed competency' = number of inversions of the best individual's structural genome (the swaps restricted bubble sort needs to reach fitness 1.0). Using the mean over repeats per generation: pass if all of (R) the mean best-individual competency first reaches 300 by generation 50; (L) its mean over generations 801-1000 is in [440, 500]; (N) that plateau mean exceeds the mean needed competency over generations 801-1000; (S) |mean over 901-1000 minus mean over 801-900| <= 20.
tests.fail: Pre-registered: refutes if the plateau mean (generations 801-1000) is < 400, or is not above the mean needed competency, or the mean best-individual competency never reaches 300. Any other failure of R/L/N/S -> mixed. Reported but not entering the verdict: the population maximum competency, the secondary best-individual definition, and the fraction of plateau generations in which >= 10% of the population has phenotypic fitness 1.0 (the tie condition the authors invoke for drift).
tests.interpretation: Simulation-result claim, tested by replication of the evolvable-competency experiment: a competency gene in [1, 500] initialised in [1, 15] (the paper's inclusive ranges; the authors' code draws [1, 14] and [1, 499]), 100 embryos, top-10% phenotypic selection, crossover with the gene in the right segment, point mutation over 51 positions with probability 0.6, 1000 generations. 'Best individual' follows the authors' Exp3 code (highest genotypic fitness); the phenotypically top-ranked individual is reported as a secondary definition. 'Needed competency' is the inversion count of the best individual's genome, the number of swaps restricted bubble sort needs to reach fitness 1.0. The drift attribution is the authors' explanation; the test reports whether its precondition (ties at phenotypic fitness 1.0 among more than 10% of the population) holds, but does not test drift directly.
tests.method: analysis.py runs 30 independent 1000-generation evolutions with an evolvable competency gene and records, each generation, the competency gene and inversion count of the highest-genotypic-fitness individual and of the top phenotypic individual, the population range of the gene, and how many embryos reach phenotypic fitness 1.0. The repeat-mean curve gives the rise time (first generation >= 300) and the plateau (mean over generations 801-1000), compared with the mean needed swaps.

measured.unit: mean competency gene of the best (highest-genotypic-fitness) individual over generations 801-1000, averaged over repeats
measured.uncertainty: SD across repeats of the per-run generation-801-1000 mean: 11.70; fixed seed

caveats: This is a replication of a simulation, not an empirical test: it shows what follows from the stated model, not what real cellular competency does.

The best individual's competency rose from about 9 to 309 by generation 5 and 443 by generation 10, then plateaued at 484.9 (generations 801-1000; per-run means 451-498), against a mean of 354.9 swaps needed (paper: ~364). Its genotypic fitness settled at 0.53 (paper: 52%).

The plateau is somewhat above the claim's ~470 and creeps up slowly (about 450-465 over generations 50-500, 485 after 800); it is inside the pre-registered 440-500 band. The paper's figure averages 10 runs in 10-generation bins, which may explain the difference.

In every plateau generation of every run at least 10% of embryos reached phenotypic fitness 1.0, so selection picks the first 10% among ties, the precondition of the authors' drift explanation. Values between the needed level and 500 are selectively neutral here. The test does not exclude other mechanisms that would push the gene higher, for example a buffer against mutations that lower structural fitness.

tests.label: Evolvable competency decouples genotypic from phenotypic fitness
tests.hypothesis: In a re-implementation of the Shreesha & Levin (2023) evolvable-competency model, the correlation between genotypic and phenotypic fitness across the individuals of a population falls from high values to about zero within about 20 generations and stays there.
tests.pass: Pre-registered design: 30 repeats x 1000 generations (the evolvable-competency simulator of levin-2023-competency-07 with independent seeds). Primary statistic, as the claim states it ('for all individuals in these populations'): each generation, the Pearson correlation across the 100 individuals between genotypic and phenotypic fitness (undefined when phenotypic fitness is constant; such generations are excluded and counted), averaged over repeats. Pass if all of: mean r at generation 1 >= 0.5; mean r over generations 21-40 <= 0.1; mean r over generations 41-1000 <= 0.1.
tests.fail: Pre-registered: refutes if the mean r over generations 21-40 or over generations 41-1000 is >= 0.3. Anything else not meeting the pass criterion -> mixed. Reported but not entering the verdict: the authors' code statistic (Pearson correlation between the repeat-mean best genotypic and best phenotypic fitness curves within 10-generation bins, NaN set to 0) and the selection differential on genotypic fitness (mean genotypic fitness of the 10 selected parents minus the population mean).
tests.interpretation: Simulation-result claim, tested by replication. The claim's text says the correlation was computed 'for all individuals in these populations', so the primary statistic is the per-generation Pearson correlation across the 100 individuals between genotypic and phenotypic fitness (on the paper's 9^x/9 scale). The authors' Exp3 code instead correlates the repeat-mean best-genotypic and best-phenotypic curves within 10-generation bins and sets undefined values to 0; that statistic is reported as secondary. 'Disrupts the ability to select the best structural genes' is the authors' interpretation; the selection differential on genotypic fitness is reported as a descriptive check.
tests.method: analysis.py runs 30 independent 1000-generation evolutions of the evolvable-competency model and, each generation, computes the Pearson correlation across the 100 individuals between genotypic and phenotypic fitness (generations with constant phenotypic fitness excluded), the authors' binned best-curve correlation, and the mean genotypic fitness of the 10 selected parents minus the population mean. Repeat-mean correlations over generations 21-40 and 41-1000 are compared with the pre-registered thresholds.

measured.unit: mean across-individual Pearson r between genotypic and phenotypic fitness, generations 41-1000, averaged over repeats
measured.uncertainty: SD across repeats of per-run generation-41-1000 mean r: 0.0138; fixed seed

caveats: This is a replication of a simulation, not an empirical test: it shows what follows from the stated model, not what real cellular competency does.

Across individuals the correlation falls from 0.997 at generation 1 to about 0.3 by generation 3 and stays there: 0.311 over generations 21-40 and 0.297 over 41-1000 (per-run SD 0.014); it never reaches 0.1. The pre-registered fail rule triggers on the 21-40 window (>= 0.3); the 41-1000 window is just below 0.3, so the outcome is close to the refute/mixed boundary, but it is not near zero.

The authors' own statistic reproduces the claim exactly (1.00 in the first bin, 0.00 in every later bin), but only because the best individual's phenotypic fitness is pinned at 1.0 in every run from generation 11 at the latest, so the within-bin correlation is undefined and their code sets it to 0. The reported drop to zero appears to be an artefact of that statistic rather than a loss of genotype-phenotype correlation in the population.

The weaker conclusion holds: selection's differential on genotypic fitness drops from 0.018 (generations 1-10) to 0.0015 (41-1000), and best genotypic fitness stays at 0.53, so selection does little to improve structural genes once competency is high. The residual 0.3 correlation is presumably carried by mutants whose competency or structural genes leave them short of fitness 1.0; this was not decomposed.
156 of 30,000 run-generations had constant phenotypic fitness and were excluded from the primary statistic.

tests.label: Keratocyte fragments migrate to the anode while whole keratocytes migrate to the cathode
tests.hypothesis: In published measurements of fish keratocytes in a direct-current electric field, intact cells move toward the cathode (positive directedness, cos theta > 0 with the cathode at 0 degrees) and cell fragments in the same field conditions move toward the anode (negative directedness).
tests.pass: Pre-registered: in the published primary measurements (Sun et al. 2013, Current Biology, doi:10.1016/j.cub.2013.02.026, or other published measurements of fish keratocytes and their fragments), at the same field strength (a) the mean directedness of intact cells is >= +0.5 and (b) the mean directedness of fragments is <= -0.3, with each mean differing from 0 at p < 0.01 (one-sample test from the reported mean, dispersion and n; if only a mean and n are reported, a sign test on n is not possible and (a)/(b) must instead be supported by a reported test of the authors).
tests.fail: Pre-registered: fragments have mean directedness >= 0 (no anodal migration) or intact cells have mean directedness <= 0 in the published measurements. Means in the right direction but below the magnitude thresholds or without p < 0.01 are pre-registered as 'mixed'. If no published numbers for both cells and fragments can be retrieved, the verdict is 'inconclusive' (data-unavailable).
tests.interpretation: Taxis direction is measured as directedness, the mean cosine of the angle between each cell's net displacement and the field vector pointing to the cathode (+1 = straight to cathode, -1 = straight to anode), as is standard in electrotaxis studies. 'Fragments' are anucleate lamellipodial fragments of the same keratocytes. The claim's source is Levin's 2024 review, which cites the primary experiment rather than reporting data, so the primary publication by a different group (Zhao and Mogilner labs) is an admissible published measurement; it is the same experiment the claim rests on, not an independent replication. The claim's interpretive part (the collective has the opposite taxis to its parts, illustrating hard-to-predict collective behaviour) is not tested beyond the sign reversal.
tests.method: analysis.py downloads the Sun et al. 2013 supplement, checks its SHA-256, extracts the text of its compressed PDF streams with the standard library and confirms that all 20 transcribed 'mean ± SE' directedness values of Table S1 (field-strength series 0-6 V/cm plus the 4 V/cm DMSO and pH 7.4 controls) occur in it. For each field strength it computes a one-sample z = mean/SE for cells and fragments and applies the pre-registered thresholds (cells >= +0.5, fragments <= -0.3, both p < 0.01), with the fail rule checked at 4 and 6 V/cm, the strengths of the paper's main experiments (Figure 1 is at 6 V/cm).

measured.unit: mean directedness (cos angle to field, + = cathode) of keratocytes and fragments at 6 V/cm (Figure 1 conditions)
measured.uncertainty: SE 0.05 each; z = 15.4 (cells), -11.8 (fragments)

caveats: The sign reversal is large and clean at the paper's working field strengths: at 6 V/cm cells average +0.77 (n = 39) and fragments -0.59 (n = 151), at 4 V/cm +0.81 and -0.65, all |z| > 5; the vehicle and pH 7.4 controls at 4 V/cm repeat it. Cells are positive and fragments negative at every field from 0.5 V/cm up.

Not an independent replication: this is the primary experiment the review cites (a different lab from Levin's, so independent of the claim's author, but the same data). Table S1 is labelled 'data from a representative experiment', so n counts cells within one experiment, not independent experiments.

The pre-registration said 'at the same field strength' without naming one; the rule was applied to every strength and is met at 4 and 6 V/cm, the strengths of the main figures. Below 2 V/cm cell directedness is weak (<= 0.2), so 'whole keratocytes migrate to the cathode' holds for fields of a few V/cm, not for every field.
Without a field, fragments show a slight anodal bias (-0.13 ± 0.05, z = -2.6), which is small compared with -0.59 at 6 V/cm.
z tests use the reported SE and treat cells as independent; raw trajectories are not deposited, so the summary statistics could not be recomputed from tracks.
Only the directional claim is tested; the interpretation that this illustrates hard-to-predict collective behaviour is not a measurable quantity here.

datasets.name: Sun et al. 2013, Current Biology 23:569-574, Supplemental Information (Table S1: directedness and speed of keratocytes and fragments under various EF conditions)

tests.label: Planarian heads degenerated by barium regenerate adapted to it via a handful of genes
tests.hypothesis: In the public RNA-seq of planarians whose heads regenerated adapted to barium chloride (GEO GSE98084), only a handful of genes are differentially expressed between barium-adapted heads and control heads, i.e. a small fraction of the expressed transcriptome.
tests.pass: Pre-registered: with the deposited per-sample expression values, comparing barium-adapted head samples with untreated control head samples (Welch t-test on log2(CPM+1) per gene, genes with mean CPM >= 1 in either group, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR), the number of genes with FDR < 0.05 and |log2 fold change| >= 1 is <= 20, and is <= 0.2% of the tested genes.
tests.fail: Pre-registered: >= 100 genes meet FDR < 0.05 and |log2 fold change| >= 1 in that comparison. Counts of 21-99 are pre-registered as 'mixed'. If either group has fewer than two replicate samples, or no per-sample quantification can be obtained or computed from the deposit, the verdict is 'inconclusive' (underpowered or data-unavailable).
tests.interpretation: Only the transcriptomic clause is tested: 'just a handful of genes up- and down-regulated' is mapped to the count of genes passing FDR < 0.05 and a two-fold change between barium-adapted and control heads, with 'handful' fixed in advance at <= 20 (the threshold proposed in the dataset-resolvability assessment). Head degeneration, complete adaptation and the claim that cells solved an unselected problem are not variables in the expression data and are not tested. The same finding is stated in levin-2023-agential-15 (Darwin's agential materials, 2023); this single test covers both claim ids and is filed under levin-2025-wisdom-05. If the deposit has additional groups (e.g. acute barium exposure before adaptation), their comparison with controls is reported as context only and does not enter the verdict. A t-test on few replicates has limited power, so the number of genes with |log2FC| >= 1 at nominal p < 0.01 is also reported as a sensitivity measure, not part of the verdict.
tests.method: fetch.py downloads the three GSE98084 supplementary workbooks and the series SOFT record; xlsx.py reads them with the standard library. analysis.py joins the two per-replicate FPKM files on transcript id (15,475 transcripts), keeps 15,446 with mean FPKM >= 1 in either group, and runs a Welch t-test on log2(FPKM+1), control (n = 2) vs BaCl2-adapted (n = 2), with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, counting FDR < 0.05 and |log2FC| >= 1. As context it also counts transcripts with q < 0.05 and |log2FC| >= 1 in the authors' pooled and per-replicate Cuffdiff tables, and transcripts that change two-fold in the same direction in both replicate pairs.

measured.unit: transcripts with BH FDR < 0.05 and |log2FC| >= 1, BaCl2-adapted vs control heads (Welch t on log2(FPKM+1), 2 vs 2)
measured.uncertainty: 2 replicates per group; Welch t-test has ~1-2 degrees of freedom and very low power

caveats: Deviation from the pre-registered rule, stated openly: the rule as written returns 'supports' (0 transcripts pass, <= 20), but the comparison could not have returned anything else. With two replicates per group the smallest FDR attainable across 15,446 transcripts was 0.11, so no transcript could reach FDR < 0.05 whatever the biology. A verdict that the data could not have contradicted is not evidence for the claim, so it is reported as inconclusive (underpowered). The pre-registration anticipated underpowering only for fewer than two replicates; it should have required a minimum attainable FDR.

The deposited data point away from 'a handful': the authors' own pooled Cuffdiff table lists 314 transcripts at q < 0.05 and >= 2-fold change (109 up, 205 down), above the pre-registered refute threshold of 100, and 1,981 transcripts change >= 2-fold in the same direction in both control/BaCl2 replicate pairs. Cuffdiff's pooled q-values model within-condition variance from only two libraries and were not the pre-registered statistic, so they do not enter the verdict, but they show that 'a handful' depends on the threshold. Counting Cuffdiff calls per replicate pair gives 4 and 18, which is near 'a handful'.
The series summary itself describes 'a number of ion translocators' and pathway-level enrichments of ~2-3-fold, which is closer to a moderate programme than to a handful of genes.
Not independent: GSE98084 is the Levin lab's own deposit for the study the claim cites (ref [66]). The reanalysis is independent of the authors' pipeline but not of their samples.

Units are Cufflinks transcripts (TCONS ids) on a D. japonica assembly, not collapsed genes; the deposited files appear pre-filtered to expressed transcripts (15,446 of 15,475 have mean FPKM >= 1). FPKM rather than counts was used, as pre-registered for deposits with only normalized values.

Only the expression clause is tested. Head degeneration, complete adaptation and the 'no evolved barium response' interpretation are not addressed. This test also covers levin-2023-agential-15, which states the same finding.

datasets.name: GEO GSE98084: Regenerative adaptation to electrochemical perturbation in planaria (Dugesia japonica heads, 2 control, 2 BaCl2-adapted; Emmons-Bell, Durant, Martyniuk, Morokuma, Levin)

tests.label: Channelopathies that cause patterning defects link developmental biology and neuroscience
tests.hypothesis: Among human disease genes in the Human Phenotype Ontology annotations, numerous ion-channel genes cause both structural patterning defects (craniofacial or limb malformation) and nervous-system phenotypes, and ion-channel disease genes carry patterning phenotypes more often than non-channel disease genes with the same depth of phenotype annotation.
tests.pass: Pre-registered: (a) at least 20 ion-channel genes (GO:0005216 ion channel activity or a descendant, any evidence, human GOA) are annotated in HPO genes_to_phenotype to both a patterning term (HP:0001999 Abnormal facial shape, HP:0000202 Orofacial cleft, HP:0001159 Syndactyly, HP:0010442 Polydactyly or HP:0009815 Aplasia/hypoplasia of the extremities, or any descendant) and a nervous-system term (HP:0000707 Abnormality of the nervous system or descendant); and (b) among all HPO-annotated genes, the Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio for carrying a patterning term, ion-channel vs non-channel genes, stratified by deciles of each gene's number of distinct HPO terms, is > 1.2 with one-sided Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel p < 0.05.
tests.fail: Pre-registered: fewer than 10 ion-channel genes meet (a); or the Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio is < 0.8 with p < 0.05 for depletion and fewer than 20 genes meet (a). Any other outcome (e.g. >= 20 such genes but no depth-adjusted enrichment, or enrichment with 10-19 genes) is pre-registered as 'mixed'.
tests.interpretation: Only the first clause is tested: 'numerous channelopathies that result in patterning defects'. 'Channelopathy' is a human disease gene (any HPO annotation) whose product has GO ion channel activity (GO:0005216, any evidence code, NOT-qualified lines removed). 'Patterning defect' is mapped to five HPO structural-malformation branches of the face and limbs, chosen because they are the craniofacial and limb patterning outcomes Levin's cited examples emphasise; brain malformations are deliberately excluded because they are also nervous-system phenotypes and would make the overlap circular. 'Numerous' is fixed at >= 20 genes. The link to neuroscience is operationalized as co-annotation with a nervous-system phenotype, and the 'deep symmetry' as enrichment of patterning phenotypes in channel genes relative to other disease genes after controlling for how heavily each gene is phenotyped (HPO term count deciles), since syndromic genes accumulate many terms. The second clause (neuroscience tools such as drugs, optogenetics and training applied to morphogenesis) is not in these databases and is not tested.
tests.method: fetch.py downloads the four files. analysis.py defines ion-channel genes as those with a non-NOT GOA molecular-function annotation to GO:0005216 or a descendant (553 genes, 209 of them HPO disease genes), keeps HPO annotations under HP:0000118 Phenotypic abnormality for 5,269 genes, and propagates each gene's terms up the is_a hierarchy. It counts channel genes annotated to both a face/limb patterning branch and HP:0000707, then compares the fraction of channel vs non-channel genes with a patterning annotation by Fisher's exact test and by a Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio with a one-sided Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel z test over ten equal-sized strata of genes ranked by number of distinct phenotype terms.

measured.unit: ion-channel disease genes with both a face/limb patterning phenotype and a nervous-system phenotype in HPO
measured.uncertainty: depth-stratified Mantel-Haenszel OR = 0.591, one-sided CMH p(enrichment) = 0.998

caveats: The literal claim holds: 59 of 209 ion-channel disease genes (28%) have a face or limb malformation in HPO, and every one of them also has a nervous-system phenotype (e.g. KCNJ2, the Andersen-Tawil gene; CACNA1C, Timothy syndrome; KCNH1, Temple-Baraitser and Zimmermann-Laband; KCNK9, Birk-Barel; NALCN; PIEZO2; TRPV4). That is well above the pre-registered 'numerous' threshold of 20.

The specific link does not hold: channel genes carry patterning phenotypes less often than other disease genes (28% vs 34%; 32% vs 41% among genes with nervous-system phenotypes), and after stratifying by annotation depth the Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio is 0.59 (one-sided CMH p = 0.002 for depletion). Patterning defects are a common feature of syndromic disease genes in general, so their presence among channelopathies is not by itself evidence of a special developmental role for ion channels. By the pre-registered rule this combination (>= 20 genes but depletion) is 'mixed', not 'supports'.

GO:0005216 with any evidence code is broad: it includes intracellular channels and some genes whose channel function is peripheral (e.g. SEC61A1, BNIP1, TMCO1, OCA2). A stricter plasma-membrane channel set could shift the odds ratio either way.

The patterning set is five face/limb malformation branches chosen in advance; 'Abnormal facial shape' contributes most genes (45) and includes mild dysmorphic features, which are common in neurodevelopmental syndromes and may be secondary to brain or muscle defects rather than primary patterning errors.

HPO reflects what clinicians record; dysmorphology is ascertained more often in syndromic, pediatric conditions than in the adult-onset arrhythmias, myotonias and epilepsies typical of channelopathies. Depth stratification addresses annotation volume, not this case-mix difference.

Human only; the claim's scope is vertebrates. The second clause (neuroscience tools applied to morphogenesis) is not tested. HPO and GOA are 'current' releases fetched at run time, so exact numbers will drift; the SHA-256 values identify the files used.
