tests.label: Aquatic mammals lack the tall withers and haunch spines of land quadrupeds
tests.hypothesis: If buoyancy has removed the tall arched neural spines over the withers and haunches, then secondarily aquatic mammals (pinnipeds, cetaceans) should show no anterior-thoracic ('withers') peak of relative neural-spine height along the thoracolumbar column, and their anterior-thoracic spines should be relatively shorter than those of terrestrial quadrupeds; the haunch (posterior lumbar) spines should likewise not be elevated.
tests.pass: Pre-registered. Per vertebra, relative spine height h = (neural spine apex to centrum reference distance) / cranial centrum height. Per species: W = mean h over T1-T4 ('withers'); P = mean h over the posterior thoracics T10-T13 (terrestrial trough region); WI = W/P ('withers index'); HI = mean h over the last three lumbars / P ('haunch index'). Test A (Carnivora landmark data, Figueirido et al. 2021): SUPPORTS-component if every pinniped species has W below the 25th percentile of terrestrial carnivoran W and one-sided Mann-Whitney U tests give p < 0.05 for pinnipeds < terrestrial on both W and WI. Test B (cetacean linear data, Gillet et al. 2019, h = Lnp/Hc; W over the first three thoracics, P over the last three thoracics, WI = W/P): SUPPORTS-component if the median cetacean WI <= 1 and at least 80% of cetacean species have WI below the minimum WI of the terrestrial carnivorans from Test A. Overall verdict 'supports' only if both components support.
tests.fail: Pre-registered. Because the claim says the spines have 'entirely disappeared' in 'all aquatic mammals', a single aquatic group retaining a terrestrial-grade withers refutes it. REFUTES if (A) any pinniped species has W >= the terrestrial carnivoran median W, or (B) at least 20% of cetacean species have WI >= the terrestrial carnivoran median WI (an anterior-thoracic peak of terrestrial proportions). If neither the supports nor the refutes conditions are met, the verdict is 'mixed'. If a required measurement (spine landmarks, Lnp or Hc) is missing from the files, that component is 'inconclusive / data-unavailable'.
tests.interpretation: Thompson's 'high arched vertebral spines over the withers' are read as a regional peak of tall neural spines in the anterior thoracic vertebrae, and the 'corresponding structures over the hind-limbs' as tall posterior lumbar (haunch) spines; 'disappeared' is read as absence of that peak relative to the posterior-thoracic trough and relative shortness compared with terrestrial relatives. Spine height is normalised by centrum height within each vertebra so that it is size-free. Pinnipeds are compared with terrestrial members of the same order (Carnivora), as the claim requires ('terrestrial relatives'). Cetaceans have no terrestrial comparator in the same dataset, so for them only the within-column profile (withers index) is compared with the terrestrial carnivoran reference distribution. Sirenians and the bird-pelvis part of the claim are not tested: no public tabular morphometric dataset covering them was identified before pre-registration; this is recorded as a caveat and the verdict is restricted to pinnipeds and cetaceans. In the landmark data the 'spine apex to centrum reference' distance is from the most distal spinous-process landmark to the centroid of the four cranial centrum-face landmarks (so it includes the neural arch), and centrum height is the largest diameter of that face; in the cetacean data it is the authors' neural-spine height (Lnp) over centrum height (Hc). Because the two definitions differ, absolute h values are not compared across datasets, only the within-column ratio WI.
tests.method: fetch.py downloads both Dryad version zips and records their SHA-256. analysis.py parses the IDAV landmark files, computes for each thoracic and lumbar vertebra the distance from the most distal spinous-process landmark to the centroid of the cranial centrum-face landmarks divided by the largest diameter of that face (h), averages h over T1-T4 (W), T10-T13 (P) and the last three lumbars, and forms WI = W/P and HI per specimen and then per species. Pinnipeds (n = 2 species) are compared with the 40 terrestrial carnivorans (otters and mink excluded from the reference set; sensitivity run includes them) by exact one-sided Mann-Whitney U tests and by position relative to the terrestrial quantiles. For the cetaceans, h = Lnp/Hc is computed for all 8722 measured vertebrae, WI = mean h of the first three thoracics / mean h of the last three thoracics per specimen, averaged per species, and compared with the terrestrial carnivoran WI distribution.

measured.unit: withers index WI (mean of the two pinniped species); terrestrial carnivoran WI min 1.238, median 1.910
measured.n: 45 carnivoran species (951 vertebrae) incl. 2 pinnipeds; 74 cetacean species (204 specimens, 8722 vertebrae)
measured.uncertainty: exact one-sided Mann-Whitney U, pinnipeds < terrestrial: W p = 0.0023, WI p = 0.0012 (n = 2 vs 40; smallest attainable p = 0.0012)

caveats: Only two pinniped species (one phocid, one otariid) are in the carnivoran dataset; sirenians are absent from both datasets, and the bird-pelvis half of the claim was not tested at all. The verdict therefore covers pinnipeds and cetaceans only, not Thompson's 'all aquatic mammals'.

The 'haunch' part is not discriminating in Carnivora: terrestrial carnivorans themselves show no posterior-lumbar spine peak (median HI 0.80 < 1), and pinniped HI falls inside the terrestrial range (p = 0.77). Thompson's haunch spines refer mainly to ungulates, for which no comparable public data were used.

Pinniped anterior-thoracic spines are reduced (W 2.3-2.7 vs terrestrial 2.6-5.3) and the withers peak is absent (WI about 1.0), but the spines have not literally 'entirely disappeared'; Otaria byronia's W lies above the lowest terrestrial species (Martes foina).

Relative spine height from landmarks includes the neural arch and depends on where the authors placed the spinous-process landmarks; the cetacean values come from a different measurement protocol, so only the within-column ratio WI is compared across datasets.
No phylogenetic comparative model was fitted (two pinniped species cannot support one); the Mann-Whitney test treats species as independent.

Semi-aquatic carnivorans (otters, mink) retain a terrestrial-grade withers index (1.6-1.7), consistent with Thompson's restriction to animals whose weight is carried by water, but they were excluded from the terrestrial reference set by a decision taken before analysis; including them does not change the result.
Gillet et al. label 74 species where the paper reports 73 (one specimen label is spelled 'Feresa_attenuta'); species means were taken as labelled.

tests.label: Cannon-bones of ox, sheep and giraffe differ by a simple one-axis stretch
tests.hypothesis: The cannon-bones (fused metacarpal III+IV, and likewise metatarsal) of ox, sheep and giraffe differ essentially only by a one-axis stretch: scaled to equal greatest length, the sheep's bone is about two-thirds and the giraffe's about one-third as broad as the ox's, and the residual shape difference after that single transverse scaling is small.
tests.pass: Pre-registered (claim supported). Using public osteometric measurements of adult metacarpals (greatest length GL and distal breadth Bd, or the same pair of dimensions however the source names them), with at least 10 specimens for ox (Bos taurus) and sheep (Ovis aries) and at least 3 for giraffe (Giraffa): the species median of Bd/GL, expressed relative to the ox, is 0.67 +/- 0.10 for sheep and 0.33 +/- 0.10 for giraffe. If 3D surface meshes rather than tables are used, GL is the maximum caliper length and Bd the maximum extent perpendicular to the long axis within the distal 15% of the bone, both computed from the mesh.
tests.fail: Pre-registered (claim refuted). Either relative breadth ratio falls outside its stated window, or (where a second breadth, e.g. mid-shaft, is available) the two breadth ratios for the same species differ by more than 0.15, which would mean a single transverse scaling does not describe the difference. If the measurements for any of the three species cannot be obtained from public sources without authentication, the verdict is 'inconclusive' with reason 'data-unavailable'.
tests.interpretation: Thompson's Fig. 346 compares the three cannon-bones drawn to the same length, so the operational quantity is breadth at equal length, i.e. the ratio Bd/GL, and the claim is about the ratio of that quantity between species (sheep/ox = 2/3, giraffe/ox = 1/3). The +/- 0.10 windows come from the within-species spread of metapodial proportions reported in zooarchaeology (breed, sex and age change Bd/GL by a few percent, not by tens of percent). Metacarpals are used because they are what Thompson figures; metatarsals would serve equally if the same three species are measured the same way. Candidate sources, to be queried in this order: MorphoSource (3D meshes), the Animal Bone Metrical Archive Project and other zooarchaeological osteometric archives (ox and sheep), Open Context zooarchaeology, FuTRES/GEOME trait records, and Zenodo/Dryad datasets. No measurements have been inspected before this pre-registration; only hit counts and HTTP status codes from catalogue searches.
tests.method: fetch.py runs the pre-registered catalogue searches and records the URL, time, HTTP status, response size, SHA-256 and hit count of each (derived/source_probe.json). Two further sources were probed with a headless Chrome browser because they return bot challenges to plain HTTP clients: the Archaeology Data Service archive page for the Animal Bone Metrical Archive Project (HTTP 403, Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' interstitial) and Open Context (Anubis challenge page, and a dropped connection from a plain client). No measurement file was downloaded, so there is nothing to analyse and no analysis.py.

measured.unit: metacarpal distal breadth / greatest length, relative to ox

caveats: No public source was found that gives cannon-bone greatest length and breadth, or a measurable 3D mesh, for all three of ox, sheep and giraffe. Ox metacarpal meshes exist on MorphoSource (5 laser scans) but sheep metacarpals return nothing there and the only giraffe media is a cranium; the single Dryad giraffe limb-bone dataset is 8.5 GB of CT imagery of metatarsals with no comparative material.

The two large zooarchaeological osteometric archives that would supply ox and sheep (the Animal Bone Metrical Archive Project at the Archaeology Data Service, and Open Context) are behind bot challenges (Cloudflare 403 and Anubis) that a headless browser did not clear in this run; even if cleared, neither contains giraffe, so the giraffe third of the claim would still be missing.

The claim is not untestable in principle: measurements of a handful of museum metapodials of the three species, or scans of them, would settle it quickly. The gap is that such measurements are not published as open data. The assessors scored 'data-existence' 0.68-0.86 largely on the expectation that MorphoSource covers ungulate metapodials; for sheep and giraffe it does not.

Hit counts in the probe log are as of 2026-10-31 and will change as catalogues grow; the Zenodo 'giraffe metacarpal' query reports 119 hits only because the terms are OR-combined across full text, and its top results are unrelated.

tests.label: Perissodactyls are more closely related to hares and rabbits than to other ungulates
tests.hypothesis: If the claim holds, Perissodactyla and Leporidae form a clade in the current synthetic mammal phylogeny that excludes the other ungulates (Artiodactyla; also Proboscidea and Hyracoidea in the 1917 sense of Ungulata) and excludes the rodents.
tests.pass: Pre-registered. Take the Open Tree of Life synthetic tree (induced_subtree API, current synth version) over these tips: Perissodactyla = Equus caballus, Ceratotherium simum, Tapirus terrestris; other ungulates = Bos taurus, Sus scrofa, Camelus dromedarius (Artiodactyla), Loxodonta africana (Proboscidea), Procavia capensis (Hyracoidea); Leporidae = Oryctolagus cuniculus, Lepus europaeus, Sylvilagus floridanus; other lagomorph = Ochotona princeps; Rodentia = Mus musculus, Rattus norvegicus, Sciurus carolinensis, Cavia porcellus, Castor canadensis; outgroups = Canis lupus, Homo sapiens, Monodelphis domestica. Let C be the smallest clade containing all perissodactyl and all leporid tips. Sub-claim 1 (perissodactyls closer to leporids than to other ungulates) holds iff C contains no artiodactyl tip; sub-claim 2 (leporids closer to perissodactyls than to other rodents) holds iff C contains no rodent tip. Supports if both hold. Independent check: NCBI Taxonomy lineages (efetch) must place Perissodactyla and Leporidae in a shared named clade below Boreoeutheria that excludes Artiodactyla and Rodentia.
tests.fail: Refutes if C contains both artiodactyl and rodent tips, i.e. perissodactyls nest with other ungulates and leporids nest with rodents rather than with each other (and NCBI Taxonomy places Perissodactyla in Laurasiatheria with Artiodactyla and Leporidae in Glires with Rodentia). Mixed if exactly one sub-claim holds.
tests.interpretation: Thompson's 'more closely related' is read as phylogenetic proximity (more recent common ancestry), the standard modern meaning and the one his transformation argument invokes. 'Other ungulates' is taken in the 1917 sense (Artiodactyla, with Proboscidea and Hyracoidea also included and reported separately); 'other rodents' means Rodentia, since lagomorphs were then classed as rodents (Duplicidentata). The Open Tree synthesis integrates published molecular phylogenies independent of the skull-shape argument; NCBI Taxonomy is a curated classification, not an independent inference, and is used only as a consistency check.
tests.method: Resolved the 20 pre-registered species to OTT ids with the Open Tree TNRS, requested the induced subtree of the current synthetic tree (synth opentree16.1), parsed the Newick, and found the smallest clade containing all three perissodactyl and all three leporid tips. Sub-claim 1 was scored by whether that clade contains artiodactyl tips, sub-claim 2 by whether it contains rodent tips; the smallest clades for perissodactyls+artiodactyls and leporids+rodents were also extracted. NCBI Taxonomy lineages were fetched by E-utilities and intersected to find named clades shared by Perissodactyla and Leporidae but not by Artiodactyla or Rodentia.

measured.unit: tips (of 20) in the smallest Open Tree clade containing all perissodactyl and leporid tips; it is Boreoeutheria and includes all artiodactyl, rodent, carnivore and primate tips
measured.uncertainty: topology from a synthesis of published phylogenies; no branch support values in the synthetic tree

caveats: The Open Tree synthetic tree carries no support values; however the groupings that refute the claim (Perissodactyla with Artiodactyla and Carnivora in Laurasiatheria; Leporidae with Ochotonidae and Rodentia in Glires) are recovered by every large molecular phylogenomic study of placental mammals and are encoded in NCBI Taxonomy, which is a curated classification rather than an independent analysis.

Thompson's claim was framed as an inference from a Cartesian transformation of skull outlines; the test addresses only its phylogenetic conclusion, not whether the skull transformation itself is geometrically simple.

Proboscidea and Hyracoidea (ungulates in the 1917 sense) fall in Afrotheria, outside the clade shared by perissodactyls and leporids, so for those 'other ungulates' sub-claim 1 would hold trivially; the sub-claim fails for the Artiodactyla, the ungulates Thompson's comparison (horses, rhinoceroses vs other hoofed mammals) most directly concerns.

The induced-subtree Newick is saved under data/ and its SHA-256 recorded; re-running against a later synth version may change the version string but not the result unless mammalian phylogeny is overturned.

tests.label: Ape and human skull differences form one continuous, roughly logarithmic transformation
tests.hypothesis: If the differences between the human skull and the chimpanzee (and baboon) skull form one continuous deformation whose grid areas 'increase in a gradual and approximately logarithmic order' from above downwards and from behind forwards, then the local area scale factor of the human-to-ape transformation of the lateral (sagittal) skull profile must be a smooth monotone function of antero-inferior position, with its logarithm roughly linear in that position, rather than a patchwork of region-specific changes.
tests.pass: Pre-registered. Primary plan (landmark coordinates available for Homo sapiens and Pan troglodytes): generalised Procrustes superimposition of all specimens; species mean configurations; projection of the means onto the midsagittal plane (midline landmarks as they are, bilateral landmarks averaged across sides) giving a lateral profile with x = antero-posterior and y = supero-inferior axes defined by the Frankfurt-like orientation of the human mean; fit a 2-D thin-plate spline mapping the human mean to the chimpanzee mean and evaluate its Jacobian determinant J (local area ratio chimpanzee/human) at every landmark of the human mean. Define the down-forward coordinate u = (x_forward + y_downward)/sqrt(2) of each landmark. The claim is supported if (a) Spearman rho(u, log J) >= 0.6 with positive sign, (b) the sign of the correlation of log J with x_forward alone and with y_downward alone is positive in both, and (c) an ordinary linear regression of log J on u explains >= 50% of the variance in log J (the 'logarithmic order' of areas, i.e. geometric progression of area ratio with grid position). Secondary plan (only inter-landmark distances available): log of the ratio of chimpanzee to human mean distance, each distance first divided by the geometric mean of all distances in its specimen; assign each distance by the anatomical names of its endpoints to one of three ordered regions (1 neurocranium/vault/occiput, 2 orbit/upper face/nasal, 3 maxilla/palate/mandible/alveolar); supported if Spearman rho(region rank, log ratio) >= 0.6 and region medians increase monotonically 1 < 2 < 3. If the data also contain Gorilla, the same statistics are reported for Gorilla as a replication but do not enter the verdict. Because baboon (Papio) data could not be located, confidence attached to any verdict is capped at 0.6.
tests.fail: Pre-registered. Refuted if Spearman rho(u, log J) < 0.3 (primary plan) or rho(region rank, log ratio) < 0.3 (secondary plan), or if the correlation of log J with x_forward and with y_downward have opposite signs (expansion forwards but contraction downwards or vice versa), or if the regression of log J on u explains < 25% of the variance while log J differs between anatomical regions in a non-monotone way (patchwork rather than gradient). Results between the pass and fail thresholds are 'mixed'. If the deposited file contains neither coordinates nor named inter-landmark distances per specimen (e.g. only summary statistics), the verdict is inconclusive with reason data-unavailable.
tests.interpretation: Thompson's grids compare lateral profile drawings of one human, one chimpanzee and one baboon skull. His claim has two parts: (1) the human-to-ape change is a single smooth deformation, not independent changes of jaws, braincase and face; (2) within that deformation the local area ratio increases 'in a gradual and approximately logarithmic order' downwards and forwards, i.e. the logarithm of the area ratio grows roughly linearly with position along the down-forward direction. Both are operationalized on species mean landmark configurations via a thin-plate spline (the modern formalisation of Thompson's coordinate transformation): smoothness and single-gradient structure are measured by how much of the variation in log local area ratio is explained by a linear gradient in down-forward position, and the 'logarithmic order' by the sign and strength of that gradient. Searches of Dryad, Zenodo and figshare on 2026-10-31 found no public per-specimen landmark set containing Papio together with Homo and Pan; MorphoSource and Phenome10K scans require a login and would also require digitising landmarks, which is beyond this test. The Zenodo deposit of Schroeder & von Cramon-Taubadel (2017, Evolution) covers 15 extant hominoid taxa including Homo and Pan; its exact contents (coordinates vs distances, per specimen vs summary) were not inspected before this pre-registration, which is why primary and secondary plans are both stated.
tests.method: The deposit holds per-specimen inter-landmark distances, not coordinates, so the pre-registered secondary plan was run. Each specimen's 39 log distances were centred on their mean (log geometric-mean size correction); species means were taken; the log ratio Pan troglodytes / Homo was formed for each distance. Each of the 21 landmarks was assigned to an ordered region of the human skull from its anatomical name (1 neurocranium/vault/cranial base: BR LD AS OPI BA JP APET EAM SP TS KR; 2 orbit/upper face/nasal/zygomatic arch: NA FM ZS ZYGO NSL; 3 maxilla/palate/alveolar: IS PM PNS MT ZI), and each distance scored by the mean of its endpoint ranks. Spearman rho between score and log ratio, medians by region and a bootstrap over specimens (2000 resamples) were computed; Gorilla and Pan paniscus were run as replications that do not enter the verdict.

measured.unit: Spearman rho (region score vs size-corrected log distance ratio Pan troglodytes/Homo)
measured.uncertainty: bootstrap 95% CI over specimens 0.664-0.732; p = 8.6e-7

caveats: Secondary (weaker) plan: the deposit gives inter-landmark distances, not landmark coordinates, so no thin-plate-spline area ratios could be computed; distance ratios are linear rather than areal scale factors and position is an ordinal three-level region score assigned by the analyst from landmark names, not a measured coordinate.

No baboon (Papio) data were available; Thompson's statement that the baboon shows 'the same order' of deformation with greater intensity is untested. Gorilla, which Thompson also mentions, shows the same gradient with a steeper slope (0.28 vs 0.22 log units per region step), consistent with his 'increased intensity' remark.

The relation is monotone and roughly linear in log ratio across region ranks (R^2 0.48 for Pan, 0.51 for Gorilla), which is what 'approximately logarithmic order' predicts, but with only three ordinal positions a linear trend cannot be distinguished from other monotone shapes.

Within the neurocranium, cranial-base distances (APET-BA, KR-SP, BA-EAM) have positive log ratios while vault distances (BR-LD, LD-AS, OPI-LD) are strongly negative, in line with Thompson's claim that the gradient runs downwards as well as forwards; this was not a pre-registered test.

Species means of adult crania of mixed sex were compared; the dataset's log distances are size-corrected by geometric mean, so the test concerns shape, whereas Thompson's figures also carried a size difference.
Spearman p-values treat the 39 distances as independent, which they are not (shared endpoints); the bootstrap CI over specimens does not address this dependence either.

tests.label: Depth expansion and lateral compression vary inversely, conserving fish volume
tests.hypothesis: Among related teleost species (same family), relative body depth (depth/length) and relative body width (width/length) vary inversely, so that the length-weight coefficient k = W/L^3, a proxy for volume at a given length, varies less across species than either relative transverse dimension.
tests.pass: Pre-registered. Species means from FishShapes v1 specimens (standard length SL, maximum body depth BD, maximum fish width FW, mass M; specimens with all four > 0). Variables per species: d = ln(BD/SL), w = ln(FW/SL), k = ln(M/SL^3). Families with >= 5 species are kept and each variable is centred on its family mean. (A) Spearman rho between family-centred d and w is < 0 with one-sided p < 0.05. (B) the SD of family-centred k is smaller than the SDs of family-centred d and of family-centred w. SUPPORTS if A and B both hold.
tests.fail: Pre-registered. REFUTES if the Spearman rho between family-centred d and w is >= 0 AND the SD of family-centred k is >= the smaller of the SDs of family-centred d and w. Any other outcome is MIXED. Fewer than 20 qualifying families or 200 species: inconclusive (underpowered).
tests.interpretation: Thompson's 'expansion in one transverse dimension compensated by compression in the other' is read as negative covariation of depth and width at a given length among related fishes; 'related' is operationalized as the same family (FishBase family names used in FishShapes). Length is standard length; 'thickness' is maximum fish width; 'volume at a given length' is mass/SL^3 (Thompson's k uses weight, so mass is the direct quantity). Family-centring removes between-family differences so that the comparison is among related species, as Thompson's haddock/plaice and shark/skate examples are. Because ln k is approximately d + w + ln(density x shape factor), condition B can hold only if d and w covary negatively; it is the 'volume less affected than the linear dimensions' clause. Secondary, reported but not part of the verdict: Thompson's named pair, plaice (Pleuronectes platessa) vs haddock (Melanogrammus aeglefinus), if both are in the data: depth ratio expected ~2, width ratio ~0.5, k ratio ~1. Note they are in different orders, so this pair is not 'related' by the family criterion.
tests.method: analysis.py downloads the Dryad version zip, verifies the specimen CSV against Dryad's SHA-256 digest, keeps the 16,377 specimens with positive mass, SL, depth and width, and takes geometric species means (6,091 species). For the 5,670 species in the 195 families with >= 5 species it computes d = ln(depth/SL), w = ln(width/SL) and k = ln(mass/SL^3), centres each on its family mean, and computes the Spearman correlation of centred d and w and the SDs of centred d, w and k. Per-family correlations and SDs are written to derived/families.csv; the plaice/haddock ratios are reported separately.

measured.unit: Spearman rho between family-centred ln(body depth/SL) and ln(body width/SL) across teleost species
measured.uncertainty: one-sided p (rho<0) = 1; 195 families with >= 5 species

caveats: Within families, relatively deep species are also relatively wide, not narrower: the family-centred correlation is +0.53, positive in 90% of the 195 families (median +0.56). As a result ln k varies more (SD 0.35) than ln depth/SL (0.22) or ln width/SL (0.18), the opposite of Thompson's 'volume less affected than the linear dimensions'.

Both ratios are divided by standard length, so overall elongation (slender vs stocky species) makes them covary positively. The pre-registered test follows Thompson's own framing ('at a given length'), but it does not isolate depth-width compensation at fixed cross-sectional area; an analysis that removes elongation (e.g. using depth/width directly or a cross-section measure) was not pre-registered and was not run.

Thompson's named pair is partly borne out: plaice is 2.09 times as deep relative to length as haddock (expected ~2) and 0.64 times as wide (expected ~0.5, inside the pre-registered 0.35-0.7 band), but its k is 1.44 times haddock's, outside the pre-registered 0.8-1.25 'nearly equal' band. This pair is descriptive only and not part of the verdict.

Specimens are preserved museum fish; mass and width can change with fixation and ethanol storage, and specimens were chosen as adult-sized, not at matched length. These add noise to k but are unlikely to reverse the sign of a +0.53 correlation across 5,670 species.
Species means rest on 1-3 specimens; intraspecific variation and measurement error inflate all three SDs, and k (three measurements combined) gets the most.

preregistered_at is the time of the pre-registration commit (78fafafa); the committed pre-registration carried an estimated time (21:40Z) written before committing. The data were first downloaded after that commit; criteria are unchanged.

tests.label: Universal computation is possible in systems with one-sentence rules
tests.hypothesis: Elementary cellular automaton rule 110, whose rule is stated in one sentence, is computationally universal (Cook 2004). The published proof is a chain of exact emulations: 2-symbol Turing machines -> 2-tag systems (Cocke/Cook, Cook 2004 section 2.1), 2-tag systems -> cyclic tag systems (Cook 2004 section 2.2), cyclic tag systems -> rule-110 glider systems (Cook 2004 sections 3-4). The first two links are fully specified constructions that can be executed and checked exactly; the third relies on the glider inventory of rule 110 (Cook 2004 figure 5), whose velocities must be present in rule-110 evolutions.
tests.pass: Pre-registered. (A) One-sentence rule: the sentence 'A cell becomes black if it or its right-hand neighbour is black, unless it and both of its neighbours are black' has at most 30 words and, evaluated as a Boolean predicate on the 8 neighbourhoods, reproduces all 8 entries of Wolfram's rule 110 (binary 01101110). (B) TM -> tag: for 30 random 2-symbol Turing machines with 2-4 states (every transition writes a bit, moves left or right, and changes to any state; no halting), each started from a random tape of 8 bits on each side of the head and run for 40 steps, Cook's 10m-symbol 2-deletion tag system (rules as printed on pp. 5-6 of Cook 2004) started from the encoded configuration reaches the encoded configuration of each successive Turing-machine step within 100000 tag steps; 100% of the 1200 step checks succeed. (C) Tag -> cyclic tag: for the same 30 tag systems plus 30 random 2-tag systems with 2-6 symbols and appendants of length 0-4, each run for 200 tag steps from a random tape (or until the tape empties), Cook's 2k-appendant cyclic tag system (symbol i -> N^(i-1) Y N^(k-i); appendants = encoded appendants then k empty ones) reproduces the encoded tag tape after every 2k cyclic-tag steps; 100% of checks. (D) Glider inventory: the velocities of all naturally occurring rule-110 gliders in Cook 2004 figure 5 (A 2/3, B -1/2, C 0, D 1/5, E and Ebar -4/15, F -1/9, G -1/3; H and the glider gun are stated by Cook not to arise naturally) are all present among the exactly periodic localized structures measured in test-data/claim-tests/wolfram-nks/wolfram2002-ch02-09/derived/measured.json (random initial conditions, 20 runs). 'Supports' requires A-D.
tests.fail: Pre-registered. 'Refutes' if A fails (rule 110 is not the stated sentence), or if B or C fails in more than 5% of checks (the printed constructions do not emulate as claimed), or if fewer than 5 of the 7 figure-5 velocities are observed in D. Other combinations are 'mixed'. The test cannot refute Cook's theorem itself; a failure of B or C would show that the printed proof as transcribed does not work, not that no one-sentence universal system exists.
tests.interpretation: The claim is an existence claim: at least one system with a one-sentence rule is universal. It is tested on its canonical instance, rule 110, by (A) checking that the rule really is one short sentence, (B, C) executing the first two reductions of Cook's published proof exactly on random instances, and (D) checking that the glider species the third reduction is built from exist with the stated velocities. Universality is taken in Cook's sense (emulation of a universal Turing machine on finite initial data, with the periodic background and periodic right-hand table data that Cook's construction uses; Neary and Woods 2006 later showed the emulation is polynomially efficient). The third link (cyclic tag system -> rule 110, Cook 2004 section 4) is not re-executed here: its initial conditions are long glider packets whose phases are specified only in the paper's figures.
tests.method: analysis.py: (A) evaluates the sentence as the predicate (c OR r) AND NOT (l AND c AND r) on all 8 neighbourhoods and compares with rule 110; (B) for 30 random 2-symbol Turing machines builds Cook's 10m-symbol 2-deletion tag system from the printed lookup-table entries (H_kz, L_kz, R_kz, R_k*, H_k, L_k, R_k), encodes the configuration as H_k1 H_k0 [L_k1 L_k0]^TL [R_k1 R_k0]^TR (with the leading H_k1 already consumed when the head reads 0), runs the tag system and records whether the encoding of each successive TM configuration appears on the tape; (C) for those 30 tag systems and 30 random 2-tag systems builds Cook's 2k-appendant cyclic tag system and checks after every 2k cyclic-tag steps that the cyclic-tag tape is the encoding of the tag tape; (D) reads the rule-110 glider velocities measured for claim wolfram2002-ch02-09 and checks each velocity of Cook's figure 5.

measured.unit: fraction of exact emulation checks passed (TM->tag and tag->cyclic tag)
measured.uncertainty: exact (deterministic)

caveats: The third link of Cook's proof (cyclic tag system -> rule 110 via glider collisions, section 4) was not executed; only the existence of the required glider species with the velocities of figure 5 was checked. Universality of rule 110 therefore rests on the published proof plus the two links verified here, which is why confidence is 0.8 rather than higher.

Deviation from the pre-registration: Cook's tag system represents the two halves of the tape in unary, so the tag tape grows like 2^(TM steps) for machines that keep moving one way. Machines were stopped once the tape would exceed 65536 symbols (16 of 30 stopped early, after 9-23 steps), giving 749 checks instead of the planned 1200. All checks performed passed; the cap was applied before seeing any outcome and is a runtime cap, not a selection on results.

The interpretation of the alignment in Cook's text (which symbol of each pair is read) was fixed by transcribing the construction and finding that the encoded configuration for a head reading 0 appears with the leading H_k1 already consumed; the check is still exact equality of the whole tape with the encoding of the independently simulated Turing machine.

'One sentence' is judged on one 21-word English sentence for rule 110; other phrasings exist. Whether 'universal' should require finite initial data with a uniform background (Cook's construction uses a periodic background and periodic right-hand data; Neary and Woods 2006 showed the emulation is polynomially efficient) is a definitional point not tested here.
Random Turing machines have no halting state; the emulation of each step is what is checked, not halting behaviour.

tests.label: A rule-90-type cellular automaton produces a nested self-similar pattern
tests.hypothesis: Rule 90 evolved from a single black cell produces a pattern in which the triangle of the first 2^k steps is composed exactly of three copies of the triangle of the first 2^(k-1) steps (one on top, two below, with an all-white inverted triangle between them), for every k up to the depth simulated, and its rows coincide with Pascal's triangle modulo 2 as tabulated independently in OEIS A001317.
tests.pass: Pre-registered: (1) for every k = 1..11 the 2^k-step triangle decomposes exactly (zero mismatching cells) into three copies of the 2^(k-1)-step triangle plus an all-white central inverted triangle; and (2) every simulated row t whose value is present in the OEIS A001317 b-file equals A001317(t) when the row's cells at positions of parity t are read as a binary number (zero mismatching rows).
tests.fail: Pre-registered: any cell of the simulated pattern violates the three-copy decomposition at some k <= 11, or any simulated row differs from the independently tabulated A001317 value.
tests.interpretation: 'Nested triangular pieces that all have exactly the same form' is operationalised as exact self-similarity under doubling: the pattern of the first 2^k steps is three translated copies of the pattern of the first 2^(k-1) steps separated by an empty (white) inverted triangle; iterated down to k = 1 this means every triangular piece is a scaled copy of the whole. The rule is the Wolfram rule 90 (new colour = XOR of the two neighbours), started from one black cell on an otherwise white infinite line, which is simulated exactly on a line wide enough that boundaries never matter. As an independent external check the rows are compared with OEIS A001317 (Sierpinski's triangle rows read as binary numbers), which is tabulated independently of any cellular-automaton code.
tests.method: analysis.py evolves rule 90 from a single black cell for 2048 steps on a 4097-cell line (boundary never reached, asserted). For k = 1..11 it reconstructs the 2^k-row triangle from three translated copies of the 2^(k-1)-row triangle (top centred, bottom copies shifted by -2^(k-1) and +2^(k-1)) over a white background and counts mismatching cells against the simulated triangle, also counting black cells inside the central inverted triangle. It then downloads the OEIS A001317 b-file (3322 terms), reads each simulated row's cells at positions x = -t, -t+2, ..., t as a binary number and compares with A001317(t) for all 2048 rows.

measured.unit: mismatching cells in the three-copy decomposition, summed over k = 1..11
measured.uncertainty: exact

caveats: Exact self-similarity was verified up to depth 2^11 = 2048 steps; the extension to all depths follows from the row formula a(t,x) = C(t,(t+x)/2) mod 2 and Lucas's theorem, which the OEIS comparison confirms independently for every simulated row but which this test does not prove.

OEIS A001317 is itself computed from Pascal's triangle mod 2, not from a cellular automaton, so the agreement is a check against an independent construction of the same mathematical object, not against a physical dataset.

tests.label: Rule 30 from a single black cell produces an irregular, complex pattern
tests.hypothesis: The space-time pattern of elementary cellular automaton rule 30 grown from a single black cell is, in its interior, neither uniform, nor repetitive (no shift-periodicity), nor nested (no self-similarity under 2x or 3x decimation), and is essentially incompressible by general-purpose compressors relative to a random pattern of the same density, whereas reference rules that are repetitive (rule 50) and nested (rule 90) are detected as such by the same measures.
tests.pass: Pre-registered. Evolve rule 30 from a single black cell for T = 4096 steps. Analysis window W: rows t in [2048, 4095], columns |x| <= 1024 (entirely inside the light cone; 2048 x 2049 cells). (0) Not uniform: black fraction in W between 0.40 and 0.60. (1) Not repetitive: on the sub-window rows [3072, 4095], |x| <= 512, the maximum over all space-time shifts (p, s) with 1 <= p <= 64 and |s| <= p of the fraction of cells with a(t, x) = a(t - p, x - s) is A_rep <= 0.75 (random pattern ~0.5; strictly periodic pattern 1.0). (2) Not nested: for decimation factors k in {2, 3} and all offsets (a, b) in {0..k-1}^2, the agreement between a(k t + a, k x + b) of the full pattern and a(t, x) of the same pattern, over t in [T/(2k), T/k), |x| <= T/(4k), has maximum A_nest <= 0.60 (rule 90 gives 1.0 for k = 2). (3) Incompressible: lzma (preset 9 extreme) and bz2 (level 9) sizes of the bit-packed window W, divided by the sizes for a Bernoulli(p) pattern of the same shape with p equal to W's black fraction (numpy PCG64, seed 20261031), are both >= 0.80. Validity controls, required for the verdict to count: rule 50 from a single cell gives A_rep >= 0.99 on its own window; rule 90 gives A_nest >= 0.99; rule 90 and rule 50 normalized lzma ratios <= 0.5; a second independent Bernoulli control gives normalized ratio within [0.97, 1.03]. Verdict 'supports' if (0)-(3) all pass and the controls hold.
tests.fail: Pre-registered. 'refutes' if black fraction in W is outside [0.2, 0.8], or A_rep >= 0.90, or A_nest >= 0.90, or either normalized compression ratio < 0.50. 'mixed' if no refuting threshold is reached but some pass condition fails (e.g. A_rep in (0.75, 0.90) or a ratio in [0.50, 0.80)). If a validity control fails, the verdict is 'inconclusive' with reason 'other'.
tests.interpretation: Wolfram contrasts rule 30 with the three kinds of simple behavior he has just shown (uniform, repetitive, nested), so 'irregular and complex with almost no overall regularity' is operationalized as the failure of a quantitative detector for each simple kind plus near-incompressibility, measured on the interior of the pattern. The interior window deliberately excludes the left and right edges, where Wolfram himself notes (p. 27) some regularity (the periodic right edge and diagonal stripes on the left); the claim is about the overall pattern, and the edges are a vanishing fraction of the light cone. Detectors are finite: A_rep only checks space-time periods up to 64 steps, A_nest only scale factors 2 and 3, and compressors only the regularities they model, so a pass is bounded non-detection, not a proof of irregularity.
tests.method: analysis.py evolves rules 30, 50 and 90 from a single black cell for 4096 steps and analyses the interior window rows 2048-4095, |x| <= 1024 (2048 x 2049 cells). It computes the black fraction; the maximum fraction of cells agreeing with a space-time shifted copy of the pattern over all shifts p <= 64, |s| <= p (on rows 3072-4095, |x| <= 512); the maximum agreement of the pattern with its own 2x and 3x decimations over all offsets; and lzma (preset 9e) and bz2 (level 9) sizes of the bit-packed window divided by those of a density-matched Bernoulli pattern. Thresholds and control requirements are those pre-registered. Run time about 30 s.

measured.unit: fractions of cells (agreement) and compressed size relative to a density-matched Bernoulli pattern
measured.uncertainty: deterministic; the Bernoulli reference varies by about 0.03 % between seeds (second control 1.000 / 1.0003)

caveats: All four pre-registered pass conditions hold and all validity controls hold: in the interior, rule 30 is half black (0.5005), no shift up to 64 steps reproduces more than 62.5 % of cells, 2x and 3x decimations agree with the pattern at chance level (0.50), and lzma/bz2 save only 12 % and 10 % relative to a random pattern of the same density.

Rule 30 is not featureless: the best shift (p = 2, s = 2, along the left-going diagonal) agrees on 62.5 % of cells rather than 50 %, and the compressors find 10-12 % redundancy. Both reflect the diagonal stripes on the left side of the pattern, which Wolfram himself notes; they are consistent with 'almost no overall regularity' but show it is not literally none.

The rule 90 control window is 98.6 % white, so its high shift agreement (0.9865) is mostly background; it is used only as the nested and compressible control, for which it is unambiguous (decimation agreement 1.0, lzma ratio 0.03).

Detectors are finite (periods <= 64, scale factors 2 and 3, two compressors on a 2048-row window); passing them is bounded non-detection of uniform, repetitive and nested structure, not a proof that rule 30 has no global regularity.

tests.label: Simple rules with simple initial conditions can yield highly complex behavior
tests.hypothesis: There exists a system with a very short rule and a trivial initial condition whose behaviour is complex by standard operational measures: elementary rule 30 (an 8-bit rule) started from a single black cell produces a centre column that is not eventually periodic, is essentially incompressible, and passes standard randomness tests, and a space-time pattern that is far less compressible than those of nested or repetitive rules of the same description length.
tests.pass: Pre-registered. Rule 30 from a single black cell on a lattice wide enough that boundaries never influence the measured cells. (a) Compressibility: the lzma-compressed size of the first 2^16 centre-column bits (packed 8 per byte) is at least 0.95 times the compressed size of 2^16 bits from os.urandom packed the same way. (b) Aperiodicity: no period p <= 2^15 holds from any offset t0 <= 2^15 within the first 2^16 centre-column bits (i.e. for every p there is a t >= 2^15 with x[t] != x[t+p]). (c) Randomness tests on the 2^16 centre-column bits: monobit frequency test p > 0.01, Wald-Wolfowitz runs test p > 0.01, chi-square test on the 256 frequencies of non-overlapping 8-bit blocks p > 0.01. (d) Pattern complexity relative to simple rules: the lzma ratio (compressed/raw bytes of the packed bit image) of the 1001-step single-cell pattern (rows of 2001 cells) is at least 5 times larger for rule 30 than for the nested rule 90 and at least 5 times larger than for the repetitive rule 250. 'Supports' requires (a)-(d). In addition the census of all 256 elementary rules by the same pattern ratio is reported (number of rules with ratio > 0.5 of rule 30's ratio), without bearing on the verdict.
tests.fail: Pre-registered. 'Refutes' (for the witness, and hence failing to confirm the existence claim) if the rule-30 centre column is eventually periodic with period <= 2^15 within 2^16 steps, or if its lzma ratio is below 0.5 of the random baseline. Other combinations are 'mixed'.
tests.interpretation: The claim is a general-principle existence statement ('can nevertheless show'); it is tested on its canonical witness, rule 30, as both assessors propose. 'Simple rule' = 8-bit rule table; 'simple initial condition' = one black cell. 'Highly complex behaviour' is operationalized as incompressibility (lzma), absence of periodicity, and passing standard randomness tests of the centre column, plus a comparison of pattern compressibility with nested (rule 90) and repetitive (rule 250) rules of identical description length. Rule numbering is Wolfram's. A single test battery is used; a sequence can be complex under these tests and simple under others (the assessors' obstacle), and the claim's 'general phenomenon' aspect is only illustrated by the census, not established.
tests.method: analysis.py evolves rule 30 from one black cell on 131075 cells for 65536 steps and records the centre column; compresses the packed bits with lzma (preset 9 extreme) and compares with 65536 bits from os.urandom; checks every period p <= 32768 from offset 32768 for a mismatch; applies the monobit, Wald-Wolfowitz runs and 8-bit block chi-square tests; evolves all 256 rules for 1000 steps on 2003 cells and computes the lzma ratio of the packed pattern, comparing rule 30 with rules 90 and 250 and counting rules whose ratio exceeds half of rule 30's.

measured.unit: lzma size of 2^16 rule-30 centre-column bits divided by lzma size of 2^16 os.urandom bits (threshold 0.95)
measured.uncertainty: exact for rule 30; urandom baseline varies by a few bytes between runs

caveats: Pre-registered criterion (b) was mis-specified at its upper end: for a period p close to 2^15 only n - p - t0 positions can be compared (one position for p = 32767, none for p = 32768), so those two periods 'pass' the literal test vacuously and analysis.py reports preregistered_verdict = 'refutes'. Every period p <= 32766 is contradicted (the hardest, p = 32764, still has a mismatch at index 32768). The post-hoc rule requires at least 64 comparisons for a period to count; under it no period passes and the verdict is 'supports'. Both outcomes are recorded in measured.extra.

The complexity tests are a specific battery (lzma, periodicity, three NIST-style tests); rule 30's centre column is known to fail no standard test at this length, but a sequence can be complex under these and simple under others. Compression ratio 1.0 relative to os.urandom means lzma found no exploitable regularity, not that none exists.

The claim is a general principle; one witness confirms the existence reading. The census shows that 9 of the 256 elementary rules (30, 45, 73, 75, 86, 89, 101, 135, 149; mostly rule 30's and rule 45's symmetry equivalents) have pattern compressibility within a factor 2 of rule 30, the median rule compressing to 0.08% of raw size.

The os.urandom baseline is non-deterministic; the rule-30 compressed size (8252 bytes for 8192 raw bytes) can be compared directly with the raw size: lzma expands it slightly, as it does for random data.

tests.label: Rule 30's center column shows no deviation from randomness over a million steps
tests.hypothesis: The first 1,000,000 values of the centre column of elementary rule 30 started from a single black cell are not eventually periodic within that range, and the bit sequence passes the NIST SP 800-22 statistical test battery at the standard significance level.
tests.pass: Pre-registered. (1) Non-repetition: for every period p in 1..500000, the final matching suffix of x[t] = x[t - p] has length less than p (no tail of the million-step sequence consists of at least two full periods of any period p <= N/2). (2) Randomness: run the following tests, implemented in numpy following NIST SP 800-22 rev. 1a, on the 1,000,000-bit sequence: frequency (monobit), block frequency (M = 128), runs, longest run of ones (M = 10000), binary matrix rank (32 x 32), discrete Fourier transform, non-overlapping template matching (m = 9, template 000000001, N = 8 blocks), overlapping template matching (m = 9, M = 1032), Maurer's universal (L = 7, Q = 1280), linear complexity (M = 500), serial (m = 16; two p-values), approximate entropy (m = 10), cumulative sums (forward and backward), random excursions (8 states) and random excursions variant (18 states), i.e. about 41 p-values. 'supports' if (1) holds, no p-value is below 1e-4, and at most 2 p-values are below 0.01 (the NIST alpha; with 41 p-values the chance of 3 or more below 0.01 under randomness is about 0.8 %). Cross-check (not part of the verdict): the first 100,000 computed bits must agree with the OEIS A051023 b-file; a disagreement means the generator is wrong and the verdict becomes 'inconclusive' with reason 'other'.
tests.fail: Pre-registered. 'refutes' if any period is found under (1), or if any p-value is below 1e-6, or if 4 or more p-values are below 0.01. Otherwise (e.g. exactly 3 p-values below 0.01, or one between 1e-6 and 1e-4) -> 'mixed'. Random-excursions tests are only applied if the number of cycles J >= 500 as NIST requires; if not applicable they are simply omitted from the count.
tests.interpretation: 'Never repeats' is read as 'is not eventually periodic within the first million steps' (an eventually periodic sequence shows at least two full periods before the end). 'Statistical tests show no meaningful deviation from perfect randomness' is read relative to the fixed, public NIST SP 800-22 battery at alpha = 0.01, as the assessors suggested; passing it cannot establish randomness, only the absence of the deviations those tests detect, so the test can refute but only weakly confirm. The battery is implemented from the NIST specification in analysis.py rather than by running the NIST C code, so the p-values are reproducible from a clean checkout.
tests.method: analysis.py evolves rule 30 from a single black cell for 10^6 steps with bit-packed numpy (uint64 words), updating only the words inside the light cone of the centre cell at the final step, and records the centre cell at every step (generation 17 s). The first 100,001 bits were compared with the OEIS A051023 b-file. Eventual periodicity was tested for every p <= 500000 by computing the length of the longest suffix with x[t] = x[t-p] using big-integer XOR, counting a period when that length is at least p and at least 64 bits. Fifteen NIST SP 800-22 statistics (frequency, block frequency M=128, runs, longest run M=10000, 32x32 matrix rank, DFT, non-overlapping template 000000001, overlapping template m=9, Maurer universal L=7/Q=1280, linear complexity M=500 via Berlekamp-Massey, serial m=16 (2), approximate entropy m=10, cumulative sums forward/backward) were implemented in numpy/scipy from the NIST specification and validated on numpy pseudo-random bits before use; random excursions were not applicable (J = 340 cycles < 500).

measured.unit: count of periods p <= 500000 with at least two full periods (>= 64 bits) at the end of the sequence; NIST p-values
measured.uncertainty: deterministic sequence; p-values are those of the NIST statistics

caveats: Deviation from the literal pre-registration, decided on synthetic random bits before the rule 30 sequence was examined: the periodicity criterion 'suffix length >= p' flags chance matches at tiny p (a random sequence ending in 0101 has two full periods of p = 2), so a minimum matching-suffix length of 64 bits was added. For rule 30 the longest periodic suffix over all p is 17 bits (at p = 166992), so the verdict is the same under either version of the criterion.

The battery is a faithful numpy re-implementation of 15 NIST SP 800-22 statistics, not the NIST reference C code; it was checked on pseudo-random input, on an LFSR of known linear complexity and on constructed periodic sequences. Every p-value lies between 0.10 and 0.82, with none below 0.01, so no test detected a deviation; passing a finite battery cannot establish 'perfect randomness', only the absence of the regularities these tests detect, and that is the scope the claim's own wording ('none of the tests I have ever done') allows.
Random excursions and random excursions variant were omitted because the sequence has only 340 zero-crossing cycles, below the 500 NIST requires.
Black-cell frequency over the million steps is 0.50077 (frequency-test p = 0.12), consistent with the claim's implicit 50/50 balance.

tests.label: Rule 110 from one black cell becomes periodic with period 240 after about 2780 steps
tests.hypothesis: Rule 110 evolved from a single black cell becomes exactly time-periodic (in the fixed frame in which the right edge of the pattern stays at x = 0) with minimal period 240 steps, and the periodic regime begins about 2780 steps after the start.
tests.pass: Pre-registered: the smallest P in 1..2000 for which a(t+P, x) = a(t, x) for every cell x in the light cone [-t, 0] and every t from some onset t0 to the end of the run equals 240, and that onset t0 (the smallest t from which the relation holds for all later t up to T - P) lies in [2500, 3060], i.e. within 10% of 2780.
tests.fail: Pre-registered: no P <= 2000 makes the pattern periodic on the light cone for the last 2000 steps of an 8000-step run and 240 is not a period even on the fixed right-edge windows [-500, 0], [-1000, 0] and [-2000, 0]; or the minimal period is not a divisor of 240; or 240 is a period but the onset lies outside [2000, 3500]. Intermediate outcomes (minimal period a proper divisor of 240; periodicity holds only on a restricted window; onset in [2000, 2500) or (3060, 3500]) are pre-registered as 'mixed'.
tests.interpretation: Rule 110 is the Wolfram rule number 110 (rule bit k = new colour for neighbourhood 4*left + 2*centre + right). From a single black cell at x = 0 the pattern occupies only x in [-t, 0] at step t (cells right of the origin stay white), so the natural fixed frame is the one in which the right edge is at rest; Wolfram's figures on pp. 32-39 are drawn in that frame. 'Behavior that repeats every 240 steps' is read as exact time-periodicity of the whole pattern inside the light cone of time t (the cells to the left of -t at time t+P are newly created stripes and are not compared). 'The outcome is finally clear after about 2780 steps' is read as the onset of this exact periodicity, with a 10% tolerance because the text says 'about'. 'One structure survives' is not quantified separately; it is covered by the periodicity of the whole interior.
tests.method: analysis.py evolves rule 110 from one black cell for 8000 steps (boundary never reached; rows 0-4 checked against the standard 1, 11, 111, 1101, 11111). Part A (pre-registered): for P = 1..2000 it tests exact fixed-frame recurrence a(t+P,x) = a(t,x) over the light cone [-t,0] and over the right-edge windows [-500,0], [-1000,0], [-2000,0] across the last 2000 steps; no P qualifies (the leading edge and the drifting structure break every fixed-frame recurrence). Part B (diagnostic, after A): the P = 240 mismatch is recounted excluding the 300 leading-edge cells, which isolates a single cluster of 9-24 cells that drifts left at -0.0846 cells/step; an exhaustive (P, shift) search in windows of +-40 and +-150 cells around that cluster finds its exact space-time period to be (213 steps, -18 cells), with (240, 0) and (240, -20) never matching; the fixed-frame recurrence of the right-edge windows [-50,0] and [-100,0] and of the stripe region is measured for P in {7, 71, 80, 213, 240, 480}, and the onset times of each regime are determined.

measured.unit: steps (exact minimal space-time period of the surviving localized structure, with a shift of -18 cells per period)
measured.uncertainty: exact (deterministic simulation)

caveats: The onset part of the claim is confirmed: the last transient collision ends at step 2819-2852 (structure regime from 2819, right-edge 240-periodicity from 2852, P = 240 mismatch count at its final level from 2831), within 3% of 'about 2780'.

The period part is only partly confirmed. In the fixed frame the whole pattern except the surviving structure's 9-24-cell neighbourhood (and the leading edge) repeats exactly every 240 steps: the right-edge region [-50,0] has exact period 240 (not 7, 71, 80 or 213), and the stripe train coming from the left has fixed-frame period 80 and lattice vector (3 steps, +2 cells), i.e. a train of speed-2/3 gliders. But the surviving structure itself drifts left at 18 cells per 213 steps and its exact space-time period is (213, -18); it is not 240-periodic in any frame, and no frame makes the whole pattern periodic. 'Behavior that repeats every 240 steps' is therefore accurate for the stripes and the right-edge interaction but not for the surviving structure.

The pre-registered primary criterion (exact recurrence on the full light cone) cannot be met by any growing pattern because the leading edge moves; this was a flaw in the pre-registration, and the diagnostic recount excluding 300 leading-edge cells was added after seeing that result. The pre-registered 'mixed' category (periodicity only on restricted windows) is what the data show.
Results are for the single evolution the claim describes; 8000 steps were simulated, so the regimes were verified over roughly 5000 steps (about 24 structure periods, 21 periods of 240).

datasets.name: Elementary cellular automaton rule 110 from a single black cell, 8000 steps (generated by analysis.py)

tests.label: Identical cell rules yield diverse behaviors through different configurations
tests.hypothesis: Under the single local rule of elementary cellular automaton rule 110, random initial configurations settle into one dominant periodic background (the 'ether') while other finite configurations embedded in it evolve as persistent localized structures with several distinct, exactly periodic signatures (different velocities), so one rule produces qualitatively different kinds of collective behavior.
tests.pass: Pre-registered. (A) Background: there is a configuration on a 14-cell ring that rule 110 maps, after 7 steps, onto a rotation of itself (a spatially 14-periodic, temporally 7-periodic background), and in 20 independent random-initial-condition runs (density 0.5, cyclic lattice of 700 cells, 3000 steps) the mean fraction of cells whose 14-cell neighbourhood matches that background (any phase) over steps 1000-3000 is at least 0.50. (B) Structures: across the same runs, tracks of non-background cells that persist for at least 300 steps and are exactly periodic (the window around the track at time t equals the window at time t+p shifted by s cells, for 5 consecutive periods) exist with at least 3 distinct velocities s/p (pairwise differing by more than 0.05 cells/step). Both (A) and (B) must hold for 'supports'.
tests.fail: Pre-registered. 'Refutes' if no 7-step periodic 14-cell background exists or the mean background fraction is below 0.25, or if fewer than 2 distinct exactly periodic localized-structure velocities are found across all runs. Anything between (background fraction 0.25-0.50, or exactly 2 velocities) is 'mixed'.
tests.interpretation: Wolfram's statement is read as an existence claim about rule 110 (his stated example): the same cell rule, applied to different local configurations, yields (i) a regular periodic background and (ii) several distinct localized structures. 'Regular background' is operationalized as a spatially and temporally periodic configuration; 'localized structure' as a bounded cluster of non-background cells that persists and is exactly periodic up to a shift, so that its velocity s/p is a rational number. Distinct velocities are taken as evidence of 'different kinds of behavior'. No reinterpretation beyond this is needed; the test is computational and the 'dataset' is generated by analysis.py.
tests.method: analysis.py enumerates all 16384 configurations of a 14-cell ring under rule 110 and finds those that return to a rotation of themselves after 7 steps; the only non-uniform orbit (14 rotations of 00010011011111, shift 0 after 7 steps, basin 51.5% of ring states) is the ether. Twenty random initial conditions on a 700-cell ring are run for 3000 steps; a cell is 'background' when its 14-cell window equals one of the ether's window codes. Non-background cells are clustered (gap <= 3), clusters are linked across steps (centre moves <= 6 cells), and each track of >= 300 steps is tested for exact periodicity (window at t equals window at t+p shifted by s for 5 consecutive periods, p <= 60). Distinct rational velocities s/p differing by > 0.05 are counted.

measured.unit: distinct localized-structure velocities (cells/step)
measured.uncertainty: exact (deterministic computation); background fraction range over runs 0.619-0.886

caveats: Background matching uses a 14-cell window, so cells within 13 cells of a structure are flagged as non-background; the 0.80 background fraction is therefore a lower bound.

Tracks that collide or split are cut, so the 143 periodic tracks are a sample, not a census, of structures; the velocities found (2/3, -1/2, 0, 1/5, -4/15, -1/3, -1/9) coincide with Cook's gliders A, B, C, D, E, G, F but that catalogue was not used in the detection.
The test covers rule 110 (Wolfram's stated example); the claim's general wording about cellular automata is supported only by this witness.

datasets.name: Elementary cellular automaton rule 110, random initial conditions (generated by analysis.py)

tests.label: Primes follow simple generating rules yet are distributed seemingly randomly
tests.hypothesis: If the claim holds, the primes below 10^8, generated by the sieve of Eratosthenes (the 'simple rule'), look random in most of a pre-declared list of statistical respects when compared with Cramer's random model (independent events with probability 1/ln n), while possibly showing structure in a minority of respects.
tests.pass: Pre-registered. Generate all primes below N = 10^8 by sieve; validate against the OEIS A000040 b-file (first 10000 primes must match exactly) and the published value pi(10^8) = 5761455 (OEIS A006880). Simulate the Cramer model on the same range with numpy seed 20261031 and run every statistic on both. Seven respects, each with a threshold for 'random-like': R1 coarse gap distribution: for primes in [N/2, N], maximum over j of |F_emp(30 j) - (1 - exp(-30 j / mean gap))| < 0.03, where F_emp is the empirical CDF of gaps; R2 Pearson correlation of consecutive gaps in [N/2, N]: |rho| < 0.05; R3 equidistribution over the four residue classes coprime to 12: maximum deviation of a class share from 1/4 below 0.005 (the Cramer model is evaluated on its own coprime-to-12 events); R4 counts of primes in consecutive disjoint intervals of length H = round(ln N) in [N/2, N]: total variation distance between the empirical count distribution and Poisson with the same mean < 0.02; R5 discrete Fourier transform of the indicator of primes among the 2^22 odd numbers just below N: ratio of the largest non-zero-frequency power to the mean power < 30 (a Gumbel-scale maximum for random indicators is about ln(2^21) ~ 15); R6 sequential compressibility: lzma size of the sequence of half-gaps (clipped at 255) in [N/2, N] divided by the lzma size of a seeded random permutation of the same sequence >= 0.98; R7 maximum over x <= N of |pi(x) - Li(x)| / sqrt(x / ln x) < 3. A respect is calibrated only if the Cramer simulation satisfies its threshold; miscalibrated respects are dropped and reported. PASS (supports) if the primes are random-like in at least (K - 2) of the K calibrated respects (so 5 of 7 if all are calibrated).
tests.fail: Pre-registered. FAIL (refutes) if the primes are random-like in at most K - 4 of the K calibrated respects (3 of 7), or if the gap sequence is plainly regular (lzma ratio of the raw half-gap byte sequence below 0.1, or a single Fourier frequency carrying more than half the non-DC spectral power). MIXED for exactly K - 3 random-like respects (4 of 7). If the OEIS validation fails the generator is wrong and the result is 'inconclusive' (other). If the OEIS files cannot be fetched, validation falls back to the published pi(10^8) value only and this is reported.
tests.interpretation: The claim's testable core is 'their distribution seems in many respects random'; the historical remark about what mathematics neglected is not tested. 'Random' is given the book's own operational meaning (p. 1067 ff.: statistical indistinguishability from a random model in specified respects) with Cramer's model as the declared random model; 'many respects' is read as a majority of a list fixed in advance, which includes respects where structure is known to exist (Fourier peaks from small moduli, finite-size Poisson deviations) so that the test can fail. Trivial sieve structure (no even primes) is removed only in R3 by restricting to classes coprime to 12; all other statistics are applied to the raw sequences.
tests.method: analysis.py sieves all primes below 10^8 (pi(10^8) = 5761455, matching OEIS A006880; first 10000 primes match the OEIS A000040 b-file), simulates Cramer's model on the same range with seed 20261031, and evaluates the seven pre-registered respects on both: coarse gap CDF versus exponential, consecutive-gap correlation, equidistribution over residues coprime to 12, Poisson fit of counts in intervals of length 18, Fourier spectrum of the prime indicator over 2^22 odd numbers below 10^8, lzma compressibility of the half-gap sequence relative to its shuffle, and the scaled fluctuation of pi(x) - Li(x). All seven thresholds were satisfied by the Cramer simulation, so all seven respects were calibrated. Runtime about 3 min.

measured.unit: respects (of 7 calibrated) in which the primes below 10^8 are random-like at the pre-registered thresholds
measured.uncertainty: with 2.76 million primes in [5x10^7, 10^8] every reported deviation from the Cramer model is far outside sampling error (the Cramer simulation gives the sampling scale)

caveats: The verdict follows the pre-registered rule (random-like in at most 3 of 7 calibrated respects). It refutes the claim as operationalised here; it does not show that primes are 'plainly regular' (the pre-registered regularity triggers did not fire: raw lzma ratio 0.55, largest Fourier peak carries 4.2% of the power).

Three of the four failures are small in magnitude and are the known arithmetic corrections to Cramer's model: the coarse gap CDF deviates from exponential by 0.036 (threshold 0.03; Hardy-Littlewood clustering of small gaps), counts in intervals of length 18 have Fano factor 0.76 instead of 1 (total variation from Poisson 0.078; Montgomery-Soundararajan variance deficit), and lzma compresses the gap sequence 3.8% better than its shuffle (threshold 2%; consecutive gaps are correlated, rho = -0.035, the Lemke Oliver-Soundararajan type bias). With thresholds of 0.05 for R1 and 0.95 for R6 the count would be 5 of 7 and the verdict 'supports'; the result is therefore threshold-sensitive and the pre-registered thresholds were strict.

The fourth failure is large: the prime indicator has a Fourier peak at period 3 (and smaller ones at other small primes) 87600 times the mean power, versus 15.5 for the Cramer model. This is the periodic sieve structure the book itself acknowledges as a regularity.

Respects in which the primes are random-like: residue classes coprime to 12 are equidistributed to 6e-5 (Chebyshev bias invisible at this scale), consecutive-gap correlation is below 0.05 in magnitude, and pi(x) - Li(x) stays within 1.3 Cramer-model standard scales (in fact the primes fluctuate less than the random model: -754 at 10^8 versus a model scale of about 2300).
Only the random-model comparison is tested; the claim's historical remark about mathematics neglecting this is outside the test.
